title.zh: 卷一百十九 列傳第六: 木華黎 博魯朮 博爾忽
title.raw: 卷一百十九 列傳第六: 木華黎 博魯朮 博爾忽 Volume 119 Biographies 6: Muqali, Bo'orchu, Borokhula

sentences.zh: 木華黎

translations.literal: Muqali
translations.idiomatic: Muqali

sentences.zh: 木華黎，劄剌兒氏，世居阿難水東。

translations.literal: Muqali, of the Jalair clan, for generations dwelt east of the Anan River.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali belonged to the Jalair clan and his family had long lived east of the Anan River.

sentences.zh: 父孔溫窟哇，以戚裏故，在太祖麾下，從平篾裏吉，征乃蠻部，數立功。

translations.literal: His father Khun-temür, by reason of being a kinsman by marriage, served under the Taizu, followed in pacifying the Merkit, campaigned against the Naiman tribes, and repeatedly achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Khun-temür, as a royal in-law, served under Genghis Khan, helped subdue the Merkits, fought the Naiman tribes, and won distinction again and again.

sentences.zh: 後乃蠻又叛，太祖與六騎走，中道乏食，擒水際橐駝殺之，燔以啖太祖。

translations.literal: Later the Naiman rebelled again; the Taizu fled with six horsemen; on the way food ran short; they seized a camel by the water's edge, killed it, roasted it, and fed the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Naiman rebelled again, Genghis Khan fled with only six riders. Food ran out on the road, so they caught a camel by the water, killed it, roasted the meat, and gave it to the khan.

sentences.zh: 追騎垂及，而太祖馬斃，五騎相顧駭愕，孔溫窟哇以所乘馬濟太祖，身當追騎，死之。

translations.literal: Pursuing horsemen were almost upon them, and the Taizu's horse died; the five riders looked at one another in alarm; Khun-temür gave the horse he rode to save the Taizu, himself blocked the pursuers, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers were closing in when the khan's horse collapsed. The five companions stared at one another in terror. Khun-temür gave Genghis Khan his own mount, stood in the path of the pursuers, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 太祖獲免。

translations.literal: The Taizu escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Genghis Khan thus escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 有子五人，木華黎其第三子也。

translations.literal: He had five sons; Muqali was his third son.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons, and Muqali was the third.

sentences.zh: 生時有白氣出帳中。

translations.literal: At his birth white vapor issued from within the tent.
translations.idiomatic: When he was born, white vapor rose from inside the tent.

sentences.zh: 神巫異之，曰：「此非常兒也。」

translations.literal: A shaman regarded it as strange and said, "This is no ordinary child."
translations.idiomatic: A shaman took it as an omen and said, "This is no ordinary child."

sentences.zh: 及長，沈毅多智略，猿臂善射，挽弓二石強。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he was deep and resolute, possessed of many stratagems, had ape-like arms and excelled at archery, and could draw a bow of two piculs' strength.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up he became grave, resolute, and resourceful. He had long arms, was a fine archer, and could draw a bow rated at two piculs.

sentences.zh: 與博爾術、博爾忽、赤老溫事太祖，俱以忠勇稱，號掇裏班曲律，猶華言四傑也。

translations.literal: Together with Bo'orchu, Borokhula, and Chilaun he served the Taizu; all were famed for loyalty and courage; they were styled the Dorben Kürü'üd, which in Chinese means the Four Heroes.
translations.idiomatic: He served Genghis Khan together with Bo'orchu, Borokhula, and Chilaun. All four were famed for loyalty and valor and were called the Dorben Kürü'üd—the Four Heroes.

sentences.zh: 太祖軍嘗失利，會大雪，失牙帳所在，夜臥草澤中。

translations.literal: The Taizu's army once suffered defeat; it happened to snow heavily; they lost the location of the royal camp; at night they lay in the marsh grass.
translations.idiomatic: Once when the khan's army had been defeated, heavy snow fell and they lost track of the royal camp, spending the night lying in the marsh grass.

sentences.zh: 木華黎與博爾術張裘氈，立雪中，障蔽太祖，達旦竟不移足。

translations.literal: Muqali and Bo'orchu spread felt cloaks, stood in the snow, and screened the Taizu; from dusk to dawn they did not shift their feet.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali and Bo'orchu spread their felt cloaks, stood in the snow to shield the khan, and from dusk until dawn did not move their feet.

sentences.zh: 一日，太祖從三十餘騎行溪谷間，顧謂曰：「此中或遇寇，當奈何？」

translations.literal: One day the Taizu rode with a little more than thirty horsemen through a stream valley and, turning back, said, "We may meet bandits here—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: One day Genghis Khan rode through a ravine with a little over thirty men. He turned and asked, "If bandits appear here, what shall we do?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「請以身當之。」

translations.literal: They replied, "We beg to take it upon our own bodies."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Let us put our bodies in their way."

sentences.zh: 既而，寇果自林間突出，矢下如雨。

translations.literal: Before long bandits indeed burst from the forest; arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Soon enough bandits did rush out of the woods, and arrows fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 木華黎引弓射之，三發中三人。

translations.literal: Muqali drew his bow and shot at them; with three shots he hit three men.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali drew his bow and shot; three arrows brought down three men.

sentences.zh: 其酋呼曰：「爾為誰？」

translations.literal: Their chief shouted, "Who are you?"
translations.idiomatic: Their leader shouted, "Who are you?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「木華黎也。」

translations.literal: He said, "Muqali."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Muqali."

sentences.zh: 徐解馬鞍持之，捍衛太祖以出，寇遂引去。

translations.literal: Slowly he unfastened his saddle and held it up, guarding the Taizu as they went out; the bandits then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He calmly unbuckled his saddle and held it up as a shield, escorting the khan out until the bandits withdrew.

sentences.zh: 克烈王可汗與乃蠻部讎戰，求援於太祖。

translations.literal: The Kerait Wang Khan fought the Naiman tribes in feud; he sought aid from the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Khan of the Kerait was at war with the Naiman and asked Genghis Khan for help.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣木華黎及博爾術等救之，盡殺乃蠻之眾於按臺之下，獲甲仗、馬牛而還。

translations.literal: The Taizu sent Muqali and Bo'orchu and others to rescue him; they killed all the Naiman forces below Antai, seized armor, weapons, horses, and cattle, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Genghis Khan sent Muqali, Bo'orchu, and others to his aid. They annihilated the Naiman army below Antai, took arms and armor, horses, and cattle, and returned.

sentences.zh: 既而王可汗謀襲太祖，其下拔臺知之，密告太祖。

translations.literal: Afterward Wang Khan plotted to attack the Taizu; his subordinate Batai learned of it and secretly informed the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wang Khan plotted to attack Genghis Khan, but his follower Batai learned of it and secretly warned the khan.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣木華黎選精騎夜斫其營，王可汗走死，諸部大人聞風款附。

translations.literal: The Taizu sent Muqali to choose elite horsemen and strike his camp by night; Wang Khan fled and died; the chieftains of the various tribes, hearing the news, came over in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Genghis Khan sent Muqali with picked cavalry to raid the camp by night. Wang Khan fled to his death, and chieftains of the tribes submitted at the first report.

sentences.zh: 歲丙寅，太祖即皇帝位，首命木華黎、博爾術為左右萬戶。

translations.literal: In the year bingyin the Taizu assumed the imperial throne and first appointed Muqali and Bo'orchu as the Left and Right Myriarchs.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingyin year Genghis Khan took the imperial throne and first appointed Muqali and Bo'orchu as the Left and Right Myriarchs.

sentences.zh: 從容謂曰：「國內平定，汝等之力居多。

translations.literal: At ease he said to them, "Within the realm things are settled—your strength accounts for most of it.
translations.idiomatic: He said to them calmly, "The realm is at peace largely because of you.

sentences.zh: 我與汝猶車之有轅，身之有臂也。

translations.literal: You and I are like a cart that has shafts, a body that has arms.
translations.idiomatic: You and I are like shafts to a cart, arms to a body.

sentences.zh: 汝等切宜體此，勿替初心。」

translations.literal: You must take this to heart and not abandon your original intent."
translations.idiomatic: Keep this firmly in mind and do not abandon your first loyalty."

sentences.zh: 金之降者，皆言其主璟殺戮宗親，荒淫日恣。

translations.literal: Those who had surrendered from Jin all said that their ruler Jing slaughtered his kinsmen and daily indulged in wanton debauchery.
translations.idiomatic: Jin defectors all said that their ruler, Emperor Xuanzong, was killing his own kin and growing more dissolute every day.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕出師有名矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Our campaign now has a righteous name."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Now I march with just cause."

sentences.zh: 辛未，從伐金，薄宣德，遂克德興。

translations.literal: In xinwei he followed in the campaign against Jin, approached Xuande, and then captured Dexing.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinwei year he joined the campaign against Jin, approached Xuande, and captured Dexing.

sentences.zh: 壬申，攻雲中、九原諸郡，拔之，進圍撫州。

translations.literal: In renshen he attacked the prefectures of Yunzhong and Jiuyuan, took them, and advanced to besiege Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In renshen he attacked Yunzhong, Jiuyuan, and other commanderies, took them, and advanced to besiege Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 金兵號四十萬，陣野狐嶺北。

translations.literal: The Jin army was said to number four hundred thousand and formed battle lines north of Yehuling.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin army was said to number four hundred thousand and drew up north of Yehuling.

sentences.zh: 木華黎曰：「彼眾我寡，弗致死力戰，未易破也。」

translations.literal: Muqali said, "They are many and we few; unless we fight with utmost resolution, they will not be easy to break."
translations.idiomatic: Muqali said, "They outnumber us. Unless we fight with everything we have, we will not break them easily."

sentences.zh: 率敢死士，策馬橫戈，大呼陷陣，帝麾諸軍並進，大敗金兵，追至澮河，僵屍百里。

translations.literal: He led dare-to-die warriors, spurred his horse with spear crosswise, shouted loudly as he charged the formation; the Emperor waved the armies forward together; they routed the Jin army greatly, pursued to the Hui River, and corpses lay stiff for a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: He led his dare-to-die troops, spurred his horse with lance leveled, and charged the line shouting. The khan ordered the whole army forward. The Jin force was routed and pursued to the Hui River, with corpses strewn for a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，攻居庸關，壁堅，不得入，遣別將阇別統兵趨紫荊口，金左監軍高琪引兵來拒，不戰而潰，遂拔涿州。

translations.literal: In guiyou he attacked Juyong Pass; the walls were strong and he could not enter; he sent the separate commander Chebie at the head of troops toward Zijingkou; the Jin Left Military Commissioner Gao Qi led troops to resist, fled without fighting, and they then took Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In guiyou he attacked Juyong Pass but could not break the strong walls. He sent the detached commander Chebie toward Zijingkou. Gao Qi, the Jin Left Military Commissioner, came to resist, fled without fighting, and Zhuozhou was taken.

sentences.zh: 因分兵攻下益都、濱、棣諸城，遂次霸州，史天倪、蕭勃叠率眾來降，並奏為萬戶。

translations.literal: Thereupon he divided the army to attack and take Yidu, Bin, and Di and other cities; then he halted at Bazhou; Shi Tianni and Xiao Bodie led the masses to surrender; both were memorialized as myriarchs.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent detachments to take Yidu, Bin, Di, and other cities, and encamped at Bazhou. Shi Tianni and Xiao Bodie surrendered with their followers, and both were recommended as myriarchs.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，從圍燕，金主請和，北還。

translations.literal: In jiaxu he followed in the siege of Yan; the Jin ruler sought peace; they returned north.
translations.idiomatic: In jiaxu he joined the siege of Yan. The Jin emperor sued for peace, and the army returned north.

sentences.zh: 命統諸軍征遼東，次高州，盧琮、金樸以城降。

translations.literal: He was ordered to command all armies in the eastern-Liao campaign; he halted at Gaozhou; Lu Cong and Jin Pu surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to command the armies in the Liaodong campaign. At Gaozhou, Lu Cong and Jin Pu surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，裨將蕭也先以計平定東京。

translations.literal: In yihai the deputy general Xiao Yexian by stratagem pacified the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In yihai the deputy commander Xiao Yexian pacified the Eastern Capital by stratagem.

sentences.zh: 進攻北京，金守將銀青率眾二十萬拒花道逆戰，敗之，斬首八萬餘級。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack the Northern Capital, the Jin defending general Yin Qing led two hundred thousand men to block the Huadao road and give battle; they defeated him and cut off more than eighty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing on the Northern Capital, he met the Jin defender Yin Qing with two hundred thousand men blocking the Huadao road. He defeated them and took more than eighty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 城中食盡，契丹軍斬關來降，進軍逼之，其下殺銀青，推寅答虎為帥，遂舉城降。

translations.literal: Food in the city was exhausted; the Khitan army cut through the pass and came to surrender; the army advanced and pressed them; his subordinates killed Yin Qing, set up Yindahu as commander, and then surrendered the whole city.
translations.idiomatic: When food in the city ran out, the Khitan troops opened the gates and surrendered. As the army closed in, Yin Qing's men killed him, made Yindahu commander, and surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 木華黎怒其降緩，欲坑之，蕭也先曰：「北京為遼西重鎮，既降而坑之，後豈有降者乎？」

translations.literal: Muqali was angry that their surrender had been slow and wished to bury them alive; Xiao Yexian said, "The Northern Capital is a great stronghold of western Liao; if after surrendering we bury them alive, will there be any who surrender afterward?"
translations.idiomatic: Muqali was angry at the delay in surrender and wanted to massacre them. Xiao Yexian said, "The Northern Capital is a major stronghold of western Liao. If we slaughter them after they surrender, who will surrender later?"

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: He followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 奏寅答虎留守北京，以吾也而權兵馬都元帥鎮之。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Yindahu should remain to guard the Northern Capital and that Uyar-edei should act as Military Commander-in-Chief to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended that Yindahu stay to guard the Northern Capital and that Uyar-edei serve as acting Military Commander-in-Chief to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 遣高德玉、劉蒲速窩兒招諭興中府，同知兀裏卜不從，殺蒲速窩兒，德玉走免。

translations.literal: He sent Gao Deyu and Liu Pusuwo'er to summon Xingzhong Prefecture; the Vice Commissioner Ulubu refused; they killed Pusuwo'er; Deyu fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Gao Deyu and Liu Pusuwo'er to win over Xingzhong Prefecture. Vice Commissioner Ulubu refused, killed Pusuwo'er, and Deyu escaped.

sentences.zh: 未幾，吏民殺兀裏卜，推土豪石天應為帥，舉城降，奏為興中尹、兵馬都提控。

translations.literal: Before long officials and people killed Ulubu, set up the local magnate Shi Tianying as commander, and surrendered the whole city; he was memorialized as Administrator of Xingzhong and Military Controller-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the officials and people killed Ulubu, made the local magnate Shi Tianying commander, and surrendered the city. Shi was recommended as prefect of Xingzhong and Military Controller-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 錦州張鯨聚眾十餘萬，殺節度使，稱臨海郡王，至是來降。

translations.literal: Zhang Jing of Jinzhou gathered a host of more than one hundred thousand, killed the military commissioner, styled himself Prince of Linhai, and at this time came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing of Jinzhou had raised more than one hundred thousand men, killed the military commissioner, and styled himself Prince of Linhai; he now came to surrender.

sentences.zh: 詔木華黎以鯨總北京十提控兵，從掇忽闌南征未附州郡。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Muqali to have Jing command the ten brigade armies of the Northern Capital and follow Doholian south to campaign against unsubmitted prefectures and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali was ordered to place Jing in command of the ten brigades of the Northern Capital and follow Doholian south against unsubmitted prefectures.

sentences.zh: 木華黎密察鯨有反側意，請以蕭也先監其軍。

translations.literal: Muqali secretly observed that Jing had intentions of wavering and requested that Xiao Yexian supervise his army.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali secretly saw that Jing was unreliable and asked that Xiao Yexian supervise his troops.

sentences.zh: 至平州，鯨稱疾逗留，復謀遁去，監軍蕭也先執送行在，誅之。

translations.literal: When they reached Pingzhou, Jing claimed illness and lingered, again plotting to flee; the supervising general Xiao Yexian seized him and sent him to the imperial camp, where he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingzhou, Jing feigned illness and lingered, plotting escape again. Supervisor Xiao Yexian seized him, sent him to headquarters, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 鯨弟致憤其兄被誅，據錦州叛，略平、灤、瑞、利、義、懿、廣寧等州。

translations.literal: Jing's younger brother Zhi, enraged that his brother had been executed, seized Jinzhou and rebelled, overrunning Ping, Luan, Rui, Li, Yi, Yi, and Guangning and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's brother Zhi, furious at his brother's execution, seized Jinzhou and rebelled, raiding Ping, Luan, Rui, Li, Yi, Yi, Guangning, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 木華黎率蒙古不花等軍數萬討之，州郡多殺致所署長吏降。

translations.literal: Muqali led several tens of thousands of troops including Mongol Buka to suppress him; many prefectures and commanderies killed the chief officials Zhi had appointed and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali led tens of thousands of men, including Mongol Buka, against him. Many prefectures killed the officials Zhi had appointed and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進逼紅羅山，主將杜秀降，奏為錦州節度使。

translations.literal: Advancing to press Hongluo Mountain, the commander Du Xiu surrendered; he was memorialized as Military Commissioner of Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing Hongluo Mountain, commander Du Xiu surrendered and was recommended as military commissioner of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙子，致陷興中府。

translations.literal: In bingzi Zhi took Xingzhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In bingzi, Zhi captured Xingzhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七月，進兵臨興中。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he advanced the army to Xingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he advanced on Xingzhong.

sentences.zh: 先遣吾也而等攻溜石山，諭之曰：「今若急攻，賊必遣兵來援，我斷其歸路，致可擒也。」

translations.literal: First he sent Uyar-edei and others to attack Liushi Mountain and instructed them, "If we press the attack now, the bandits will surely send troops to relieve it; we cut off their return route and Zhi can be captured."
translations.idiomatic: He first sent Uyar-edei to attack Liushi Mountain and told them, "If we press hard now, the rebels will send reinforcements. We can cut off their retreat and capture Zhi."

sentences.zh: 又遣蒙古不花屯永德縣東候之。

translations.literal: He also sent Mongol Buka to encamp east of Yongde County and wait for them.
translations.idiomatic: He also posted Mongol Buka east of Yongde County to wait for them.

sentences.zh: 致果遣鯨子東平將騎兵八千、步卒三萬，援溜石。

translations.literal: Zhi indeed sent Jing's son Dongping leading eight thousand cavalry and thirty thousand infantry to relieve Liushi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi did send Jing's son Dongping with eight thousand cavalry and thirty thousand infantry to relieve Liushi.

sentences.zh: 蒙古不花引兵趨之，馳報，木華黎夜半引兵疾馳，遇於神水縣東，夾擊之。

translations.literal: Mongol Buka led troops toward them and sent a swift report; Muqali at midnight led troops in rapid march; they met east of Shenshui County and attacked from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol Buka moved to intercept and sent word. Muqali marched through the night and met the enemy east of Shenshui County, attacking from both sides.

sentences.zh: 分麾下兵之半，下馬步戰。

translations.literal: He divided half of the troops under his command, dismounted, and fought on foot.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered half his force to dismount and fight on foot.

sentences.zh: 選善射者數千，令曰：「賊步兵無甲，疾射之！」

translations.literal: He chose several thousand skilled archers and ordered, "The bandits' infantry have no armor—shoot them swiftly!"
translations.idiomatic: He picked several thousand good archers and ordered, "The enemy infantry have no armor—shoot them fast!"

sentences.zh: 乃麾騎兵齊進，大敗之，斬東平及士卒萬二千八百餘級。

translations.literal: Then he waved the cavalry forward together; they routed them greatly; they cut off Dongping and more than twelve thousand eight hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Then he led the cavalry forward in a charge. The enemy was routed; Dongping and more than twelve thousand eight hundred soldiers were killed.

sentences.zh: 拔開義縣，進圍錦州。

translations.literal: They took Kaiyi County and advanced to besiege Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: They took Kaiyi County and advanced to besiege Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 致遣張太平、高益出戰，又敗之，斬首三千餘級，溺死者不可勝數。

translations.literal: Zhi sent Zhang Taiping and Gao Yi out to give battle; they were again defeated; more than three thousand heads were cut off; those who drowned were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi sent Zhang Taiping and Gao Yi out to fight. They were defeated again; more than three thousand were killed and countless men drowned.

sentences.zh: 圍守月餘，致憤將校不戮力，殺敗將二十餘人。

translations.literal: After more than a month of siege, Zhi, angry that officers did not exert themselves, killed more than twenty defeated generals.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month under siege, Zhi, angry that his officers were not trying hard enough, executed more than twenty defeated commanders.

sentences.zh: 高益懼，縛致出降，伏誅。

translations.literal: Gao Yi was afraid, bound Zhi and brought him out to surrender; he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yi, in fear, bound Zhi and surrendered him. Zhi was executed.

sentences.zh: 廣寧劉琰、懿州田和尚降，木華黎曰：「此叛寇，存之無以懲後。」

translations.literal: Liu Yan of Guangning and the monk Tian of Yizhou surrendered; Muqali said, "These are rebel bandits; if we spare them there is no way to warn those who come after."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan of Guangning and Tian the Monk of Yizhou surrendered. Muqali said, "These are rebels. If we spare them, there will be no warning for others."

sentences.zh: 除工匠優伶外，悉屠之。

translations.literal: Apart from artisans and entertainers, all were slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Except for artisans and entertainers, all were put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 拔蘇、復、海三州，斬完顏眾家奴。

translations.literal: They took the three prefectures Su, Fu, and Hai and beheaded Wanyan Zhongjianu.
translations.idiomatic: They took Su, Fu, and Hai prefectures and beheaded Wanyan Zhongjianu.

sentences.zh: 咸平宣撫薄鮮等率眾十餘萬，遁入海島。

translations.literal: Bo Xian and others, Pacification Commissioners of Xianping, led a host of more than one hundred thousand and fled to sea islands.
translations.idiomatic: Bo Xian and other pacification commissioners of Xianping led more than one hundred thousand men and fled to the islands.

sentences.zh: 丁丑八月，詔封太師、國王、都行省承制行事，賜誓券、黃金印曰：「子孫傳國，世世不絕。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month of dingchou an edict enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor, King, and Chief Secretariat with authority to act by imperial commission; he was granted a covenant tablet and a golden seal reading, "Descendants shall transmit the state; generation after generation without end."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of dingchou he was enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor and King, given a Secretariat with full commission, a covenant tablet, and a golden seal inscribed, "Descendants shall hold this fief forever."

sentences.zh: 分弘吉剌、亦乞烈思、兀魯兀、忙兀等十軍，及吾也而契丹、蕃、漢等軍，並屬麾下。

translations.literal: Ten armies including Hongjila, Yiqiliesi, Ulugu, and Mangwu, together with Uyar-edei's Khitan, Fan, and Han armies, were all placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Ten armies—the Hongjila, Yiqiliesi, Ulugu, Mangwu, and others—together with Uyar-edei's Khitan, tribal, and Han forces were all placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 且諭曰：「太行之北，朕自經略，太行以南，卿其勉之。」

translations.literal: Moreover he instructed, "North of the Taihang Mountains I myself shall plan; south of the Taihang Mountains, you must exert yourself."
translations.idiomatic: He also told him, "North of the Taihang Mountains I will manage myself; south of them, you must do your utmost."

sentences.zh: 賜大駕所建九斿大旗，仍諭諸將曰：「木華黎建此旗以出號令，如朕親臨也。」

translations.literal: He granted the nine-tassel great banner built for the imperial carriage and further instructed the generals, "When Muqali raises this banner to issue commands, it is as if I were present in person."
translations.idiomatic: He gave him the nine-tassel banner of the imperial guard and told the generals, "When Muqali raises this banner to command, it is as if I were there myself."

sentences.zh: 乃建行省於雲、燕，以圖中原，遂自燕南攻遂城及蠡州諸城，拔之。

translations.literal: He then established a Secretariat at Yun and Yan to plan for the Central Plain; then from south of Yan he attacked Suicheng and Lizhou and other cities and took them.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a Secretariat at Yun and Yan to conquer the Central Plain, then attacked Suicheng, Lizhou, and other cities south of Yan and took them.

sentences.zh: 冬，破大名府，遂東定益都、淄、登、萊、濰、密等州。

translations.literal: In winter he broke Daming Prefecture, then secured to the east Yidu, Zi, Deng, Lai, Wei, and Mi and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he took Daming Prefecture, then secured Yidu, Zi, Deng, Lai, Wei, Mi, and other prefectures to the east.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，自西京由太和嶺入河東，攻太原、忻、代、澤、潞、汾、霍等州，悉降之。

translations.literal: In wuyin from the Western Capital he entered Hedong by Taihe Ridge, attacked Taiyuan, Xin, Dai, Ze, Lu, Fen, Huo, and other prefectures, and all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In wuyin he left the Western Capital, entered Hedong by Taihe Ridge, attacked Taiyuan, Xin, Dai, Ze, Lu, Fen, Huo, and other prefectures, and all submitted.

sentences.zh: 遂徇平陽，金守臣棄城遁，以前鋒拓拔按察兒統蒙古軍鎮之拒金兵，以義州監軍李廷植之弟守忠權河東南路帥府事。

translations.literal: Then he marched on Pingyang; the Jin defending official abandoned the city and fled; the vanguard Tabo Ancha'er commanded Mongol troops to garrison it and resist Jin troops; Li Shouzhong, younger brother of the Yizhou Military Supervisor Li Tingzhi, was made acting commander of the Hedong South Circuit headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He then marched on Pingyang. The Jin defender fled. The vanguard Tabo Ancha'er garrisoned it with Mongol troops to hold off Jin forces, and Li Shouzhong, brother of Yizhou supervisor Li Tingzhi, was made acting commander of the Hedong South Circuit.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以蕭特末兒等出雲、朔，攻降岢嵐火山軍。

translations.literal: In jimao Xiao Temu'er and others went out from Yun and Shuo and attacked and reduced Kelan Huoshan Army.
translations.idiomatic: In jimao, Xiao Temu'er and others left Yun and Shuo, attacked, and reduced Kelan Huoshan Army.

sentences.zh: 以谷裏夾打為元帥達魯花赤，攻拔石、隰州，擊絳州，克之。

translations.literal: Gulijada was made Commander darughachi; he attacked and took Shi and Xi prefectures, struck Jiangzhou, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Gulijada was made commander darughachi, took Shi and Xi prefectures, attacked Jiangzhou, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，復由燕徇趙，至滿城。

translations.literal: In gengchen he again from Yan marched through Zhao to Mancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In gengchen he again marched from Yan through Zhao to Mancheng.

sentences.zh: 武仙舉真定來降。

translations.literal: Wu Xian raised Zhending and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian surrendered Zhending.

sentences.zh: 權知河北西路兵馬事史天倪進言曰：「今中原粗定，而所過猶縱兵抄掠，非王者吊民之意也。」

translations.literal: Shi Tianni, acting Administrator of Hebei West Circuit Military Affairs, advanced and said, "Now the Central Plain is roughly settled, yet wherever the army passes it still allows troops to plunder—this is not the intent of a king who comes to comfort the people."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tianni, acting administrator of Hebei West Circuit military affairs, urged him, "The Central Plain is largely pacified, yet troops still plunder wherever they march. That is not how a true king comforts his people."

sentences.zh: 木華黎曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Muqali said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: Muqali said, "You are right."

sentences.zh: 下令禁無剽掠，所獲老稚，悉遣還田里，軍中肅然，吏民大悅。

translations.literal: He issued an order forbidding plunder; all old and young who had been taken were sent back to their villages and fields; the army became orderly; officials and people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered an end to looting, sent all captured old and young back to their villages, and the army became disciplined. Officials and people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 兵至滏陽，金邢州節度使武貴迎降，進攻天平寨，破之。

translations.literal: When the army reached Fuyang, the Jin Military Commissioner of Xingzhou Wu Gui came out to welcome and surrender; they advanced to attack Tianping Stockade and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: At Fuyang the Jin military commissioner of Xingzhou, Wu Gui, surrendered. They attacked Tianping Stockade and took it.

sentences.zh: 遣蒙古不花分兵略定河北衛、懷、孟州，入濟南。

translations.literal: He sent Mongol Buka to divide troops and pacify Wei, Huai, and Meng prefectures of Hebei, and enter Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Mongol Buka with detachments to secure Wei, Huai, and Meng in Hebei and enter Jinan.

sentences.zh: 嚴實籍所隸相、魏、磁、名、恩、博、滑、浚等州戶三十萬，詣軍門降。

translations.literal: Yan Shi registered the households of the thirty prefectures under his jurisdiction—Xiang, Wei, Ci, Ming, En, Bo, Hua, and Jun and others, three hundred thousand households—and came to the army gate to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi registered three hundred thousand households in Xiang, Wei, Ci, Ming, En, Bo, Hua, Jun, and other prefectures under his rule and came to the camp to surrender.

sentences.zh: 時金兵屯黃陵岡，號二十萬，遣步兵二萬襲濟南。

translations.literal: At that time Jin troops were encamped at Huanglinggang, said to number two hundred thousand; they sent twenty thousand infantry to raid Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin forces were then encamped at Huanglinggang, said to number two hundred thousand, and sent twenty thousand infantry to raid Jinan.

sentences.zh: 木華黎以輕兵五百擊走之。

translations.literal: Muqali with five hundred light troops struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali routed them with five hundred light troops.

sentences.zh: 遂會大軍，薄黃陵岡。

translations.literal: Then he joined the great army and pressed Huanglinggang.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the main army and closed on Huanglinggang.

sentences.zh: 金兵陣河南岸，示以死戰。

translations.literal: The Jin army formed battle lines on the south bank of the river, showing they would fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin army drew up on the south bank of the river, ready to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 木華黎曰：「此不可用長兵，當以短兵取勝。」

translations.literal: Muqali said, "Here one cannot use long weapons; one must use short weapons to win."
translations.idiomatic: Muqali said, "Long weapons will not work here. We must win with short weapons."

sentences.zh: 令騎下馬，引滿齊發，亦下馬督戰，果大敗之，溺死者眾。

translations.literal: He ordered the cavalry to dismount, draw to the full and release together; he also dismounted to direct the battle; they indeed routed them greatly; many drowned.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the cavalry to dismount, draw their bows full, and shoot together, then dismounted himself to direct the fight. The Jin force was routed and many drowned.

sentences.zh: 進攻楚丘。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Qiuqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to attack Qiuqiu.

sentences.zh: 楚丘城小而固，四面皆水，令諸軍以草木填塹，直抵城下。

translations.literal: Qiuqiu was small but solid; on all four sides there was water; he ordered the armies to fill the moat with grass and wood and go straight to below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Qiuqiu was small but strong and surrounded by water on all sides. He ordered the troops to fill the moat with brush and timber and reach the walls.

sentences.zh: 嚴實率所部先登，拔之。

translations.literal: Yan Shi led his own troops in the first ascent and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi's men were first over the wall and the city was taken.

sentences.zh: 攻下單州，圍東平，以實權山東西路行省，戒之曰：「東平糧盡，必棄城走，汝伺其去，即入城安輯之，勿苦郡縣，以敗事也。」

translations.literal: He attacked and took Danzhou, besieged Dongping, made Shi acting Shandong West Circuit Secretariat, and admonished him, "When Dongping's grain is exhausted they will surely abandon the city and flee; you watch for their departure, then enter the city and settle and comfort it; do not harass the prefectures and counties and ruin the affair."
translations.idiomatic: He took Danzhou and besieged Dongping, making Yan Shi acting Shandong West Circuit Secretariat. He warned him, "When Dongping runs out of food they will flee. Wait until they leave, then enter and pacify the city. Do not harass the counties or you will ruin everything."

sentences.zh: 留梭魯忽禿以蒙古軍三千屯守之。

translations.literal: He left Soluqutu with three thousand Mongol troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: He left Soluqutu with three thousand Mongol troops to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 辛巳四月，東平糧盡，金行省忙古奔汴，梭魯忽禿邀擊之，斬七千餘級，忙古引數百騎遁去。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of xinsi, Dongping's grain was exhausted; the Jin Secretariat Manggu fled to Bian; Soluqutu intercepted and struck them, cutting off more than seven thousand heads; Manggu led several hundred horsemen and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of xinsi, Dongping ran out of food. The Jin Secretariat Manggu fled to Bianjing. Soluqutu intercepted him, killed more than seven thousand men, and Manggu escaped with only a few hundred riders.

sentences.zh: 實入城，建行省，撫其民。

translations.literal: Shi entered the city, established a Secretariat, and comforted the people.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi entered the city, set up a Secretariat, and pacified the people.

sentences.zh: 先是，郡王帶孫攻洺不下，至是遣石天應拔之。

translations.literal: Earlier the Prince of the Domain Toqto had attacked Ming without success; at this time he sent Shi Tianying to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Prince Toqto had failed to take Mingzhou; he now sent Shi Tianying, who captured it.

sentences.zh: 五月，還軍野狐嶺。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the army returned to Yehuling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the army returned to Yehuling.

sentences.zh: 宋漣水忠義統轄石珪來降，以為濟、兗、單三州都總管，予繡衣玉帶，勞之曰：「汝不憚跋涉數千里，慕義而來，尋當列奏，賜汝高爵，爾其勉之。」

translations.literal: Song Lianshui Righteousness Command overseer Shi Gui came to surrender; he was appointed Grand Commander of the three prefectures Ji, Yan, and Shan; given brocade robes and a jade belt; consoled him, saying: "You did not shrink from traveling several thousand li, came drawn by righteousness — soon I shall submit a memorial and bestow on you high rank; exert yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Gui, commander of the Righteousness militia at Lianshui under the Song, surrendered. Muqali appointed him Grand Commander of Ji, Yan, and Shan prefectures, granted him brocade robes and a jade belt, and encouraged him: "You have traveled thousands of li without flinching, drawn by loyalty to our cause. I shall soon petition the throne to reward you with high office. Do your utmost."

sentences.zh: 京東安撫使張琳皆來降，以琳行山東東路益都滄景濱棣等州都元帥府事。

translations.literal: Jingdong Pacification Commissioner Zhang Lin also came to surrender; Lin was appointed to administer the eastern Shandong route Grand Marshal headquarters for Yidu, Cang, Jing, Bin, Di, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Jingdong Pacification Commissioner Zhang Lin surrendered as well. Zhang Lin was put in charge of the eastern Shandong Grand Marshal headquarters at Yidu, Cang, Jing, Bin, Di, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 鄭遵亦以棗鄉、蓧縣降，升為元州，以遵為節度使，行元帥府事。

translations.literal: Zheng Zun also surrendered with Zaoxiang and Diaoxian; the area was elevated to Yuan Prefecture; Zun was made Military Commissioner and exercised Grand Marshal headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zun also submitted Zaoxiang and Diaoxian. The district was raised to Yuan Prefecture, and Zheng Zun was made Military Commissioner with authority over the Grand Marshal headquarters.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，從駐青冢，監國公主遣使來勞，大饗將士，由東勝渡河，西夏國李王請以兵五萬屬焉。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn, following the encampment at Qingzhong, the Regency Princess sent envoys to express sympathy; a great feast was held for officers and soldiers; they crossed the river from Dongsheng; Western Xia Prince Li requested to place fifty thousand troops under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Muqali followed the khan's camp at Qingzhong. The Regency Princess sent envoys with gifts for the army, and he held a great feast for his officers and men. Crossing the river from Dongsheng, Prince Li of Western Xia offered fifty thousand troops to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，復由雲中歷太和寨，入葭州，金將王公佐遁，以石天應權行臺兵馬都元帥。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, again from Yunzhong via Taihe Stockade, entered Jia Prefecture; Jin general Wang Gongzuo fled; Shi Tianying was appointed acting Secretariat Cavalry Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he again marched from Yunzhong through Taihe Stockade into Jia Prefecture. The Jin general Wang Gongzuo fled, and Shi Tianying was made acting Cavalry Grand Marshal of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 進取綏德，破馬蹄寨，距延安三十里止舍。

translations.literal: Advanced to take Suide, broke Matai Stockade, halted encampment thirty li from Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Suide, captured Matai Stockade, and encamped thirty li from Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 金行省完顏合達出兵三萬陣於城東，蒙古不花以騎三千覘之，馳報曰：「彼見吾兵少，有輕敵心，明日合戰，當佯敗，可以伏兵取勝也。」

translations.literal: Jin Secretariat Wanyan Heda led thirty thousand troops arrayed east of the city; Mongol Buka with three thousand cavalry reconnoitered and sent a swift report, saying: "They see our troops are few and despise us. In tomorrow's battle we should feign defeat; then ambush troops can win."
translations.idiomatic: Jin Secretariat Wanyan Heda drew up thirty thousand men east of the city. Mongol Buka rode out with three thousand cavalry to scout and sent word back: "The enemy sees how few we are and will fight carelessly. Tomorrow we should pretend to flee in battle; then our ambush can finish them."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Muqali agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali agreed.

sentences.zh: 夜半以大軍銜枚齊進，伏於城東十五里兩谷間。

translations.literal: At midnight the main army advanced together with gags in their mouths and lay in ambush in two valleys fifteen li east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight the main army moved up in silence and hid in two valleys fifteen li east of the city.

sentences.zh: 明日，蒙古不花進兵，望見金兵，即棄鼓旗走。

translations.literal: The next day Mongol Buka advanced; upon seeing the Jin troops he immediately abandoned drums and banners and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Mongol Buka advanced, and as soon as he sighted the Jin army he dropped drums and banners and fled.

sentences.zh: 金兵果追之，伏發，鼓聲震天地，萬矢齊下，金兵大敗，斬七千級，獲馬八百。

translations.literal: The Jin troops indeed pursued; the ambush sprang; drum sounds shook heaven and earth; ten thousand arrows fell together; the Jin army was greatly defeated; seven thousand heads were cut; eight hundred horses were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin force pursued as expected. The ambush struck, drums thundered, and arrows fell in sheets. The Jin army was routed: seven thousand were killed and eight hundred horses taken.

sentences.zh: 合達走保延安，圍之旬日，不下，乃南徇洛川，克鄜州。

translations.literal: Heda fled to hold Yan'an; it was besieged ten days without success; then he marched south through Luochuan and captured Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Heda fled into Yan'an. After a ten-day siege failed to take the city, Muqali turned south through Luochuan and captured Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 北京權帥石天應擒送金驍將張鐵槍，木華黎責其不降，厲聲答曰：「我受金朝厚恩二十餘年，今事至此，有死而已！」

translations.literal: Beijing acting commander Shi Tianying captured and sent the fierce Jin general Zhang Tieqiang; Muqali reproached him for not surrendering; he answered in a loud voice: "I received the Jin dynasty's generous grace for more than twenty years; now matters have come to this — only death!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tianying, acting commander of Beijing, captured the fierce Jin general Zhang Tieqiang and brought him in. Muqali rebuked him for refusing to submit. Zhang answered boldly: "The Jin court showed me favor for more than twenty years. Now that it has come to this, I ask only to die!"

sentences.zh: 木華黎義之，欲解其縛，諸將怒其不屈，竟殺之。

translations.literal: Muqali admired his righteousness and wished to release his bonds; the generals, angry at his refusal to submit, in the end killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali admired his loyalty and wanted to free him, but the other generals, enraged by his defiance, killed him anyway.

sentences.zh: 遂降坊州，大饗士卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fang Prefecture surrendered; a great feast was held for the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Prefecture then surrendered, and Muqali held a great feast for his troops.

sentences.zh: 聞金復取隰州，以軒成為經略使，於是復由丹州渡河圍隰，克之。

translations.literal: He heard the Jin had retaken Xi Prefecture and appointed Xuan Cheng Pacification Commissioner; thereupon again crossed the river from Dan Prefecture to besiege Xi and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the Jin had retaken Xi Prefecture and put Xuan Cheng in charge as Pacification Commissioner, he crossed the river again from Dan Prefecture, besieged Xi, and captured it.

sentences.zh: 留合醜統蒙古軍鎮石、隰間，以田雄權元帥府事。

translations.literal: He left Hechou to command Mongol troops garrisoning between Shi and Xi; Tian Xiong was appointed acting Grand Marshal headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He left Hechou with Mongol troops to guard the region between Shi and Xi, and put Tian Xiong in charge of the Grand Marshal headquarters.

sentences.zh: 壬午秋七月，令蒙古不花引兵出秦隴，以張聲勢。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn in renwu, Mongol Buka was ordered to lead troops out of Qin-Long to display military prestige.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of renwu, Muqali ordered Mongol Buka to march into Qin and Long to make a show of force.

sentences.zh: 視山川險夷，大兵道雲中，攻下孟州四蹄寨，遷其民於州。

translations.literal: Surveying mountains and rivers for ease and danger, the main army went via Yunzhong, attacked and took Meng Prefecture Siti Stockade, and relocated its people to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After surveying the terrain, the main army went by way of Yunzhong, took Siti Stockade in Meng Prefecture, and resettled its people in the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 拔晉陽義和寨，進克三清巖，入霍邑山堡，遷其人於趙城縣。

translations.literal: He took Jinyang Yihe Stockade, advanced and captured Sanqing Cliff, entered Huoyi mountain fort, and relocated its people to Zhaocheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Yihe Stockade at Jinyang, took Sanqing Cliff, seized the mountain fort at Huoyi, and moved its inhabitants to Zhaocheng County.

sentences.zh: 薄青龍堡，金平陽公胡天作拒守，裨將薄察定住、監軍王和開壁降，遷天作於平陽。

translations.literal: Approaching Qinglong Fort, Jin Prince of Pingyang Hu Tianzuo resisted and defended; subordinate generals Bocha Dingzhu and supervisory commissioner Wang He opened the walls and surrendered; Tianzuo was relocated to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: At Qinglong Fort, Hu Tianzuo, Prince of Pingyang, held out against him, but his subordinates Bocha Dingzhu and the supervisory commissioner Wang He opened the gates and surrendered. Hu Tianzuo was sent to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 八月，有星晝見，隱士喬靜真曰：「今觀天象，未可征進。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month a star appeared in daytime; recluse Qiao Jingzhen said: "Observing the heavens now, one must not advance on campaign."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month a star appeared in daylight. The recluse Qiao Jingzhen said, "The heavens now warn against advancing."

sentences.zh: 木華黎曰：「主上命我平定中原，今河北雖平，而河南、秦、鞏未下，若因天象而不進兵，天下何時而定耶？

translations.literal: Muqali said: "Our lord ordered me to pacify the Central Plains; now though Hebei is pacified, Henan, Qin, and Gong are not yet taken; if because of heavenly signs we do not advance troops, when will the realm be settled?
translations.idiomatic: Muqali replied, "The khan ordered me to pacify the Central Plains. Hebei is secure, but Henan, Qin, and Gong still hold out. If we halt every time the sky sends a sign, when will the empire ever be settled?

sentences.zh: 且違君命，得為忠乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover, to violate the lord's command — can that be loyalty!"
translations.idiomatic: And would it be loyal to disobey our lord's command?"

sentences.zh: 冬十月，過晉至絳，拔榮州胡瓶堡，所至望風歸附，河中久為金有，至是復來歸。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he passed through Jin to Jiang, took Rong Prefecture Huping Fort; wherever he went they submitted at first report; Hedong had long been Jin territory, and at this time again came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he marched through Jin to Jiang and took Huping Fort in Rong Prefecture. Everywhere he went, cities surrendered at the first approach. Hedong, long held by the Jin, now submitted once more.

sentences.zh: 木華黎召石天應謂曰：「蒲為河東要害，我擇守者，非君不可。」

translations.literal: Muqali summoned Shi Tianying and said: "Pu is the strategic key of east Hedong; of those I choose to defend it, none but you will do."
translations.idiomatic: Muqali summoned Shi Tianying and told him, "Pu is the linchpin of eastern Hedong. I can find no one better than you to hold it."

sentences.zh: 乃以天應權河東南北路陜右關西行臺，平陽李守忠、太原攸哈剌拔都、隰州田雄，並受節制。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tianying was appointed acting east Hedong north-south route Shaanxi-west Guanxi Secretariat; Pingyang Li Shouzhong, Taiyuan Yohaqar Badu, and Xi Prefecture Tian Xiong were all placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: He then made Shi Tianying acting chief of the east Hedong and Shaanxi-west Guanxi Secretariat, with Li Shouzhong at Pingyang, Yohaqar Badu at Taiyuan, and Tian Xiong at Xi Prefecture all under his authority.

sentences.zh: 命天應造浮梁，以濟歸師，乃渡河拔同州，下蒲城，徑趨長安。

translations.literal: He ordered Tianying to construct a pontoon bridge to ferry the returning army; then crossed the river, took Tong Prefecture, descended on Pucheng, and struck directly for Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali ordered Tianying to build a pontoon bridge for the returning army, then crossed the river himself, took Tong Prefecture and Pucheng, and pushed straight toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 金京兆行省完顏合達擁兵二十萬固守，不下。

translations.literal: Jin Jingzhao Secretariat Wanyan Heda with two hundred thousand troops stubbornly defended; the city could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Heda of the Jin Jingzhao Secretariat held the city with two hundred thousand men and could not be dislodged.

sentences.zh: 乃分麾下兀胡乃、太不花兵六千屯守之。

translations.literal: Thereupon six thousand troops under Uhuni and Taibuhua were detached to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali left six thousand men under Uhuni and Taibuhua to keep the siege.

sentences.zh: 遣按赤將兵三千斷潼關，遂西擊鳳翔。

translations.literal: He sent Aqchi with three thousand troops to block Tong Pass; then struck west at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Aqchi with three thousand men to seal Tong Pass, then marched west against Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 月餘不下，謂諸將曰：「吾奉命專征，不數年取遼西、遼東、山東、河北，不勞余力；

translations.literal: More than a month passed without success; he said to the generals: "I received orders for exclusive campaigns; within a few years I took Liaoxi, Liaodong, Shandong, and Hebei without extra effort;
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month the city still held. He told his generals, "I was sent to conquer on my own. In only a few years I took Liaoxi, Liaodong, Shandong, and Hebei almost without strain;

sentences.zh: 前攻天平、延安，今攻鳳翔皆不下，豈吾命將盡耶！」

translations.literal: Previously attacking Tianping and Yan'an, now attacking Fengxiang — all cannot be taken; has my allotted span neared its end!"
translations.idiomatic: yet Tianping and Yan'an resisted me before, and now Fengxiang will not fall. Has my time run out?"

sentences.zh: 乃駐兵渭水南，遣蒙古不花南越牛嶺關，徇宋鳳州而還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he encamped south of the Wei River; sent Mongol Buka south over Niuling Pass, raided Song Feng Prefecture, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He then camped south of the Wei River and sent Mongol Buka south over Niuling Pass to raid Feng Prefecture under the Song before returning.

sentences.zh: 時中條山賊侯七等聚眾十餘萬，伺大兵既西，謀襲河中。

translations.literal: At the time Zhongtiao Mountain bandits Hou Qi and others gathered more than one hundred thousand; watching the main army had gone west, they plotted to raid Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Hou Qi and other bandits of the Zhongtiao Mountains mustered more than a hundred thousand men. Seeing the main army march west, they planned a strike on Hedong.

sentences.zh: 石天應遣別將吳權府引兵五百夜出東門，伏兩谷間，戒之曰：「候賊過半，急擊之，我出其前，爾攻其後，可克也。」

translations.literal: Shi Tianying sent detached general Wu Quanfu to lead five hundred troops by night out the east gate and lie in ambush in two valleys; he warned him: "Wait until more than half the bandits pass, then strike urgently; I will go out before them and you attack from behind — then they can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tianying sent the detached commander Wu Quanfu with five hundred men out the east gate by night to hide in two valleys. He instructed him: "When more than half the enemy have passed, hit them hard. I will meet them from the front while you fall on their rear, and we shall destroy them."

sentences.zh: 吳權府醉酒失期，天應戰死。

translations.literal: Wu Quanfu, drunk, missed the appointed time; Tianying died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Quanfu got drunk and missed the signal. Shi Tianying was killed in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 城陷，賊燒毀廬舍，殺掠人民，還走中條。

translations.literal: The city fell; the bandits burned houses, killed and plundered the people, and fled back to Zhongtiao.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell. The bandits burned buildings, slaughtered and looted the people, and withdrew into the Zhongtiao range.

sentences.zh: 先鋒元帥按察兒邀擊，敗之，斬數萬級，侯七復遁去。

translations.literal: Vanguard Grand Marshal Ancar intercepted and struck, defeated them, cut tens of thousands of heads; Hou Qi again fled.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard Grand Marshal Ancar intercepted them, routed the force, and killed tens of thousands. Hou Qi escaped again.

sentences.zh: 木華黎以天應子斡可襲領其眾。

translations.literal: Muqali had Tianying's son Woke inherit command of his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali had Shi Tianying's son Woke succeed to his command.

sentences.zh: 癸未春，師還，浮梁未成，顧諸將曰：「橋未畢工，安可坐待乎！」

translations.literal: In the spring of guiwei the army returned; the pontoon bridge was not finished; he looked at the generals and said: "The bridge is not complete — how can we sit and wait!
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of guiwei, as the army withdrew, the pontoon bridge was still unfinished. Muqali told his generals, "We cannot sit idle while the bridge remains unfinished!

sentences.zh: 復攻下河西堡寨十餘。

translations.literal: Again he attacked and took more than ten fort stockades west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked again and captured more than ten fortresses west of the river.

sentences.zh: 三月，渡河，還聞喜縣，疾篤，召其弟帶孫曰：「我為國家助成大業，擐甲執銳垂四十年，東征西討，無復遺恨，第恨汴京未下耳，汝其勉之！」

translations.literal: In the third month he crossed the river and returned to Wenxi County; gravely ill, he summoned his brother Toqto and said: "I helped the state accomplish the great enterprise; wore armor and wielded sharp weapons for nearly forty years; east campaigns and west expeditions — I have no lingering regret, only regret that Bianjing is not taken; you exert yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he crossed the river and returned to Wenxi County. Mortally ill, he called his brother Toqto and said, "I have served the state for nearly forty years in armor and at the front, campaigning east and west. I leave nothing undone except the capture of Bianjing. You must finish what I could not."

sentences.zh: 薨，年五十四。

translations.literal: He died; age fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 厥後太祖親攻鳳翔，謂諸將曰：「使木華黎在，朕不親至此矣。」

translations.literal: Thereafter Taizu personally attacked Fengxiang and said to the generals: "If Muqali were alive, I would not have come here in person."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Genghis Khan personally besieged Fengxiang, he told his generals, "If Muqali were still alive, I would not have had to come myself."

sentences.zh: 至治元年，詔封孔溫窟哇推忠效節保大佐運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、魯國王，謚忠宣；

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi an edict enfeoffed Khun-temür as Merit Lord of Loyalty, Fidelity, Preservation of Greatness, and Assistance to the Dynasty — Grand Preceptor, Grand General with Honored Chancellery, Upper Pillar of State, King of Lu — posthumous title Zhongxuan;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizhi an edict posthumously enfeoffed Khun-temür as Merit Lord of Loyal Fidelity, Preservation of Greatness, and Assistance to the Dynasty, with the ranks of Grand Preceptor, Grand General with Honored Chancellery, and Upper Pillar of State, as King of Lu, with the posthumous title Zhongxuan;

sentences.zh: 木華黎體仁開國輔世佐命功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、魯國王，謚忠武。

translations.literal: Muqali as Merit Lord of Benevolent Governance, Founding the State, Assisting the Age, and Aiding Destiny — Grand Preceptor, Grand General with Honored Chancellery, Upper Pillar of State, King of Lu — posthumous title Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: and Muqali as Merit Lord of Benevolent Governance, Founding the State, Assisting the Age, and Aiding Destiny, with the same ranks, as King of Lu, with the posthumous title Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 子孛魯嗣。

translations.literal: His son Boluo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Boluo succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 孛魯，沈毅魁傑，寬厚愛人，通諸國語，善騎射，年二十七，入朝行在所。

translations.literal: Boluo was stern, resolute, and outstanding, generous and loving toward people, versed in various national languages, skilled at mounted archery; at age twenty-seven he attended court at the mobile imperial residence.
translations.idiomatic: Boluo was grave, resolute, and imposing, generous and humane, fluent in several languages, and an expert archer on horseback. At twenty-seven he presented himself at the khan's mobile court.

sentences.zh: 時太祖在西域，夏國主李王陰結外援，蓄異圖，密詔孛魯討之。

translations.literal: At the time Taizu was in the Western Regions; Western Xia Prince Li secretly allied with external aid and harbored rebellious designs; he secretly ordered Boluo to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Genghis Khan was then campaigning in the west. Prince Li of Western Xia was secretly seeking foreign allies and plotting rebellion, and the khan quietly ordered Boluo to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 甲申秋九月，攻銀州，克之，斬首數萬級，獲生口馬駝牛羊數十萬，俘監府塔海，命都元帥蒙古不華將兵守其要害而還。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn in jiashen he attacked Yin Prefecture and captured it; tens of thousands of heads were cut; live captives, horses, camels, cattle, and sheep numbering hundreds of thousands were taken; supervisory commissioner Tahai was captured; Grand Marshal Mongol Buka was ordered to lead troops to garrison strategic points, and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of jiashen he attacked and captured Yin Prefecture, killing tens of thousands and taking hundreds of thousands of captives and livestock. He seized the supervisory commissioner Tahai, left Grand Marshal Mongol Buka to hold the key points, and returned.

sentences.zh: 乙酉春，復朝行在所。

translations.literal: In the spring of yiyou he again attended court at the mobile imperial residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of yiyou he again attended the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 同知真定府事武仙叛，殺都元帥史天倪，脅居民遁於雙門寨。

translations.literal: Associate prefect of Zhending Wu Xian rebelled, killed Grand Marshal Shi Tianni, coerced the residents, and fled to Shuangmen Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian, associate prefect of Zhending, rebelled, killed Grand Marshal Shi Tianni, drove the people before him, and withdrew to Shuangmen Stockade.

sentences.zh: 仙弟質於軍中，挈家逃歸，遣撒寒追及於紫荊關，斬之，命天倪弟天澤代領帥府事。

translations.literal: Xian's younger brother was held hostage in the army; he took his family and escaped home; Saqan was sent in pursuit, caught up at Zijing Pass, and beheaded him; Tianni's younger brother Tianze was ordered to succeed to command of the marshal headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian's brother, held hostage in the Mongol camp, fled home with his family. Boluo sent Saqan in pursuit, caught him at Zijing Pass, and executed him, then put Shi Tianni's brother Tianze in charge of the marshal headquarters.

sentences.zh: 丙戌夏，詔封功臣戶口為食邑，曰十投下，孛魯居其首。

translations.literal: In the summer of bingxu an edict enfeoffed merit lords with registered households as fiefs, called the Ten Appanages; Boluo ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of bingxu an edict granted registered households as fiefs to the great merit lords, forming the Ten Appanages, with Boluo first among them.

sentences.zh: 宋將李全陷益都，執元帥張琳送楚州。

translations.literal: Song general Li Quan seized Yidu, captured Grand Marshal Zhang Lin, and sent him to Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Li Quan took Yidu, captured Grand Marshal Zhang Lin, and sent him to Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，郡王帶孫率兵圍全於益都。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn Prince of the Domain Toqto led troops to besiege Quan at Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Prince Toqto besieged Li Quan at Yidu.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，孛魯引兵入齊，先遣李喜孫招諭全，全欲降，部將田世榮等不從，殺喜孫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter Boluo led troops into Qi; first he sent Li Xisun to summon and persuade Quan; Quan wished to surrender; subordinate generals Tian Shirong and others refused and killed Xisun.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Boluo entered Qi with his army. He first sent Li Xisun to negotiate Li Quan's surrender. Quan was willing, but his officers Tian Shirong and others refused and killed Xisun.

sentences.zh: 丁亥春三月，全突圍欲走，邀擊大敗之，斬首七千餘級，自相蹂踐溺死不可勝計。

translations.literal: In the third month of spring in dinghai Quan broke out of encirclement wishing to flee; he was intercepted and greatly defeated; more than seven thousand heads were cut; trampled and drowned one another beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of dinghai Li Quan tried to break out and flee. Boluo intercepted him, inflicting a crushing defeat: more than seven thousand were killed, and countless others trampled or drowned one another in the rout.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，城中食盡，全降。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer food in the city was exhausted and Quan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, with provisions exhausted, Li Quan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆曰：「全勢窮出降，非心服也，今若不誅，後必為患。」

translations.literal: All the generals said: "Quan at the end of his strength came out to surrender — he is not sincerely convinced; if he is not executed now, later he will surely be a calamity."
translations.idiomatic: The generals all said, "Li Quan surrendered only because he was cornered, not because he submits in heart. If we spare him now, he will become a threat later."

sentences.zh: 孛魯曰：「不然，誅一人易耳。

translations.literal: Boluo said: "Not so — to execute one person is easy.
translations.idiomatic: Boluo replied, "No. Killing one man is easy enough.

sentences.zh: 山東未降者尚多，全素得人心，殺之不足以立威，徒失民望。」

translations.literal: Those in Shandong not yet surrendered are still many; Quan has always won people's hearts; killing him is not enough to establish authority and would only lose popular esteem."
translations.idiomatic: Many places in Shandong have not yet submitted. Li Quan has long enjoyed the people's trust. Executing him would not make us feared; it would only cost us their goodwill."

sentences.zh: 表聞，詔孛魯便宜處之。

translations.literal: A memorial was sent to court; an edict authorized Boluo to act as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Boluo reported to the throne, and an edict gave him discretion in the matter.

sentences.zh: 乃以全為山東淮南楚州行省，鄭衍德、田世榮副之，郡縣聞風款附，山東悉平。

translations.literal: Thereupon Quan was appointed Shandong-Huainan-Chuzhou Secretariat; Zheng Yande and Tian Shirong were made deputies; prefectures and counties submitted at first report; all Shandong was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Li Quan to the Shandong-Huainan-Chuzhou Secretariat, with Zheng Yande and Tian Shirong as his deputies. Prefectures and counties submitted one after another, and all Shandong was pacified.

sentences.zh: 子七人：長塔思，次速渾察，次霸都魯，次伯亦難，次野蔑幹，次野不幹，次阿裏乞失。

translations.literal: He had seven sons: the eldest Tarsi, next Suqunchar, next Badar, next Boyinaq, next Yemiegan, next Yebuqan, and next Ariqishi.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons: Tarsi, Suqunchar, Badar, Boyinaq, Yemiegan, Yebuqan, and Ariqishi.

sentences.zh: 塔思，一名查剌溫，幼與常兒異，英才大略，綽有祖風。

translations.literal: Tarsi — also called Char Temür — from childhood was unlike ordinary children; he had outstanding talent and broad vision and fully possessed his grandfather's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Tarsi, also known as Char Temür, was unlike other boys from childhood — gifted, far-sighted, and very much in the mold of his grandfather.

sentences.zh: 木華黎常曰：「成吾誌必此兒也。」

translations.literal: Muqali often said: "To fulfill my ambition must be this child."
translations.idiomatic: Muqali often said, "This boy will finish what I began."

sentences.zh: 及長，每語必先忠孝，曰：「大丈夫受天子厚恩，當效死行陣間，以圖報稱，安能委靡茍且目前，以隳先世勛業哉！」

translations.literal: When grown, in every conversation he put loyalty and filial piety first, saying: "A great man receiving the Son of Heaven's generous grace ought to offer his life in battle ranks to repay merit — how can he languish in shabby temporary survival and ruin the meritorious achievements of former generations!"
translations.idiomatic: As he grew up he spoke always of loyalty and filial duty. "A man who has received the emperor's great favor," he said, "should die fighting to repay it. How can he drift through life in comfort and squander the honors won by his forebears?"

sentences.zh: 年十八襲爵，遂至雲中。

translations.literal: At age eighteen he inherited the title and then went to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he inherited the title and went to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 庚寅秋九月，叛將武仙圍潞州，太宗命塔思救之，仙聞之，退軍十餘里。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn in gengyin rebel general Wu Xian besieged Lu Prefecture; Emperor Taizong ordered Tarsi to rescue it; Xian, upon hearing this, withdrew ten-odd li.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of gengyin the rebel Wu Xian besieged Lu Prefecture. Emperor Taizong ordered Tarsi to relieve the city, and Wu Xian withdrew more than ten li on hearing of his approach.

sentences.zh: 大兵未至，塔思率十餘騎覘賊形勢，仙恐有伏，不敢犯。

translations.literal: The main army had not yet arrived; Tarsi led ten-odd riders to reconnoiter the bandit positions; Xian feared ambush and dared not attack.
translations.idiomatic: Before the main force arrived, Tarsi rode out with a dozen men to scout the enemy. Wu Xian suspected an ambush and would not engage.

sentences.zh: 塔思曰：「日暮矣，待明旦擊之。」

translations.literal: Tarsi said: "The day is ending; wait until tomorrow morning to strike."
translations.idiomatic: Tarsi said, "It is growing late. We shall attack at dawn."

sentences.zh: 是夜五鼓，金將移剌蒲瓦來襲，我師與戰不利，退守沁南。

translations.literal: That night at the fifth watch Jin general Yelü Puwa came to raid; our army fought unfavorably and withdrew to defend south of the Qin River.
translations.idiomatic: That night, at the fifth watch, the Jin general Yelü Puwa launched a surprise attack. Tarsi's force fought poorly and fell back to the south bank of the Qin River.

sentences.zh: 賊還攻潞州，城陷，主將任存死之。

translations.literal: The bandits returned to attack Lu Prefecture; the city fell; commander Ren Cun died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then turned back on Lu Prefecture. The city fell, and its commander Ren Cun was killed.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，帝親征，遣萬戶因只吉臺與塔思復取潞州，仙夜遁，邀擊之，斬首七千餘級，以任存侄代領其眾。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter the Emperor personally campaigned; he sent Myriarch Inzhigetai and Tarsi to retake Lu Prefecture; Xian fled by night; they intercepted and struck; more than seven thousand heads were cut; Ren Cun's nephew was appointed to succeed to command of his forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the emperor marched in person. He sent the myriarch Inzhigetai and Tarsi to retake Lu Prefecture. Wu Xian fled by night, but they intercepted his force and killed more than seven thousand. Ren Cun's nephew was put in command of the garrison.

sentences.zh: 十一月，帝攻鳳翔，命塔思守潼關以備金兵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the Emperor attacked Fengxiang and ordered Tarsi to guard Tong Pass against Jin troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, as the emperor besieged Fengxiang, he ordered Tarsi to hold Tong Pass against Jin reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 河中自石天應死，復為金有。

translations.literal: Hedong, since Shi Tianying's death, had again become Jin territory.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong had returned to Jin control after Shi Tianying's death.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，帝親攻拔之，金元帥完顏火燎遁，塔思追斬之。

translations.literal: In xinmao the Emperor personally attacked and took it; Jin Grand Marshal Wanyan Huoliao fled; Tarsi pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In xinmao the emperor took it in person. The Jin marshal Wanyan Huoliao fled, and Tarsi pursued and killed him.

sentences.zh: 壬辰春，睿宗與金兵相拒於汝、漢間，金步騎二十萬，帝命塔思與親王按赤臺、口溫不花合軍先進渡河，以為聲援。

translations.literal: In the spring of renchen Emperor Ruizong confronted Jin troops between Ru and Han; Jin infantry and cavalry numbered two hundred thousand; the Emperor ordered Tarsi with Imperial Prince Aqchatai and Kewen Buka to combine armies, advance first, cross the river, and serve as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of renchen Emperor Ruizong faced two hundred thousand Jin foot and horse between the Ru and Han rivers. The khan ordered Tarsi, Prince Aqchatai, and Kewen Buka to join forces, cross the river first, and support the main attack.

sentences.zh: 至三峰山，與睿宗兵合。

translations.literal: They reached Sanfeng Mountain and combined with Ruizong's army.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Sanfeng Mountain and united with Ruizong's army.

sentences.zh: 金兵成列，將戰，會大雪，分兵四出，塔思冒矢石先挫其鋒，諸軍繼進，大敗金兵，擒移剌蒲瓦。

translations.literal: The Jin troops formed ranks and were about to battle; heavy snow fell; troops were divided in four directions; Tarsi braved arrows and stones and first blunted their vanguard; all armies followed advancing; the Jin army was greatly defeated; Yelü Puwa was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin army drew up for battle just as a heavy snow began. Forces were sent out on four sides. Tarsi charged through arrow and stone fire to break their front, and the other units followed until the Jin force was shattered and Yelü Puwa was taken.

sentences.zh: 完顏合達單騎走鈞州，追斬之，遂拔鈞州。

translations.literal: Wanyan Heda fled alone on horseback to Jun Prefecture; he was pursued and beheaded; thereupon Jun Prefecture was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Heda fled alone toward Jun Prefecture. Tarsi ran him down and killed him, and Jun Prefecture fell.

sentences.zh: 三月，帝北還，詔塔思與忽都虎統兵，略定河南，諸郡皆降，惟汴京、歸德、蔡州未下。

translations.literal: In the third month the Emperor returned north; an edict ordered Tarsi and Qutuqu to command troops to pacify Henan; all commanderies surrendered; only Bianjing, Guide, and Caizhou were not taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the emperor withdrew north and ordered Tarsi and Qutuqu to pacify Henan. Every commandery submitted except Bianjing, Guide, and Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 塔思遣使請曰：「臣之祖父，佐興大業，累著勛伐。

translations.literal: Tarsi sent an envoy to petition: "My grandfather and father assisted in raising the great enterprise and repeatedly achieved meritorious campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Tarsi sent a petition: "My grandfather and father helped build the empire and won honor after honor in its service.

sentences.zh: 臣襲世爵，曾無寸效，去歲復失利上黨，罪當萬死，願分攻汴城一隅，以報陛下。」

translations.literal: I inherited the hereditary title yet have achieved not an inch of merit; last year I again lost at Shangdang — the crime deserves ten thousand deaths; I wish to be assigned to attack one corner of the Bian city wall to repay Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: I inherited their rank but have done nothing worthy of it. Last year I failed at Shangdang and deserve death a thousand times over. Grant me one section of the walls of Bian to assault, that I may repay Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝壯其言，命卜之，不利，乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor admired his words, ordered divination, found it unfavorable, and thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved by his words and ordered divination, but the omens were bad, so the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 癸巳秋九月，從定宗於潛邸，東征，擒金咸平宣撫顏萬奴於遼東。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn in guisi he followed Emperor Dingzong from his princely residence on an eastern campaign and captured Jin Xianping Pacification Commissioner Yan Wannu in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of guisi he accompanied Emperor Dingzong from his princely residence on an eastern campaign and captured the Jin Xianping Pacification Commissioner Yan Wannu in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 萬奴自乙亥歲率眾保東海，至是平之。

translations.literal: Wannu since the yihai year had led masses defending the East Sea; at this time he was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wannu had held the East Sea region since yihai; now he was finally subdued.

sentences.zh: 甲午秋七月，朝行在所。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn in jiawu he attended court at the mobile imperial residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of jiawu he attended the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 時諸王大會，帝顧塔思曰：「先皇帝肇開大業，垂四十年。

translations.literal: At the time all the princes held a great assembly; the Emperor looked at Tarsi and said: "The late emperor inaugurated the great enterprise, spanning nearly forty years.
translations.idiomatic: At a great gathering of the princes, the emperor turned to Tarsi and said, "The late emperor founded this enterprise nearly forty years ago.

sentences.zh: 今中原、西夏、高麗、回鶻諸國皆已臣附，惟東南一隅，尚阻聲教。

translations.literal: Now the Central Plains, Western Xia, Goryeo, Uyghur, and all states have submitted; only the southeastern corner still blocks our transforming influence.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Central Plains, Western Xia, Goryeo, the Uyghurs, and the rest have all submitted. Only the southeast still stands outside our rule.

sentences.zh: 朕欲躬行天討，卿等以為何如？」

translations.literal: I wish to personally carry out Heaven's punitive expedition — what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: I mean to lead the punitive campaign myself. What do you advise?"

sentences.zh: 群臣未對，塔思對曰：「臣家累世受恩，圖報萬一，正在今日。

translations.literal: The ministers had not answered; Tarsi replied: "My house for generations received grace; to repay even one ten-thousandth — today is the time.
translations.idiomatic: Before the others could speak, Tarsi answered, "My family has owed the throne a debt for generations. If there is any day to repay it, it is today.

sentences.zh: 臣雖駑鈍，願仗天威，掃清淮、浙，何勞大駕親臨不測之地哉！」

translations.literal: Though I am dull and slow, I wish to rely on Heaven's authority to sweep clear Huai and Zhe — why trouble the imperial carriage to come in person to an unpredictable place!"
translations.idiomatic: I may be slow-witted, but let me carry Heaven's authority into Huai and Zhe and clear them. Why should Your Majesty risk yourself in uncertain country?"

sentences.zh: 帝悅曰：「塔思雖年少，英風美績，簡在朕心，終能成我家大事矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor, pleased, said: "Though Tarsi is young, his heroic spirit and fine achievements are known to my heart; in the end he can accomplish our family's great enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and said, "Tarsi is still young, but his courage and record are already clear to me. In time he will finish the great work of our house."

sentences.zh: 賜黃金甲、玻璃帶及良弓二十，命與王子曲出總軍南征。

translations.literal: He granted a golden armor, a glass belt, and twenty fine bows, and ordered him together with Prince Kochu to command the army on the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him with golden armor, a glass belt, and twenty fine bows, then ordered him and Prince Kochu to lead the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 乙未冬，拔棗陽。

translations.literal: In the winter of yiwei they captured Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in yiwei, they took Zaoyang.

sentences.zh: 曲出別徇襄、鄧，塔思引兵攻郢。

translations.literal: Kochu separately marched against Xiang and Deng; Tarsi led troops to attack Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Kochu swept Xiang and Deng on his own while Tarsi marched on Ying.

sentences.zh: 郢瀕漢江，城堅兵精，且多戰艦。

translations.literal: Ying bordered the Han River; its walls were strong, its soldiers elite, and it moreover had many war vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Ying lay on the Han River, strongly walled, well garrisoned, and stocked with warships.

sentences.zh: 塔思命造木筏，遣汶上達魯花赤劉拔都兒將死士五百，乘筏進擊。

translations.literal: Tarsi ordered wooden rafts built and sent the Wenshang darughachi Liu Badu'er with five hundred death-defying soldiers to advance and strike aboard rafts.
translations.idiomatic: Tarsi had rafts built and sent the Wenshang darughachi Liu Badu'er with five hundred picked men to attack by water.

sentences.zh: 引騎兵沿岸迎射，大破之，溺死者過半，餘皆走郢，壁堅，不能下，俘生口、馬牛數萬而還。

translations.literal: He led cavalry along the shore to meet them with arrow fire and routed them utterly; more than half drowned; the rest all fled to Ying; the walls were strong and could not be taken; he captured living captives and cattle in the tens of thousands and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry along the bank showered them with arrows and broke them completely. More than half drowned; the survivors fled into Ying, whose walls held firm. He withdrew with tens of thousands of captives and livestock.

sentences.zh: 丙申冬十月，復出鄧州，遂至蘄、黃。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in bingshen he again advanced from Deng Prefecture and thereupon reached Qi and Huang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of bingshen he marched out of Deng again and pushed as far as Qi and Huang.

sentences.zh: 蘄州遣使獻金帛、牛酒犒師，請曰：「宋小國也，進貢大朝有年矣。

translations.literal: Qizhou sent envoys offering gold, silk, cattle, and wine to provision the army, pleading: "Song is a small state; for years it has paid tribute to the great court.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhou sent tribute of gold, silk, cattle, and wine with a plea: "Song is a small kingdom that has paid tribute to your court for years.

sentences.zh: 惟王以生靈為念。」

translations.literal: We ask only that Your Highness bear the common people in mind."
translations.idiomatic: Spare the people, we beseech you."

sentences.zh: 乃捨之。

translations.literal: He thereupon spared them.
translations.idiomatic: Tarsi relented and spared the city.

sentences.zh: 遂進拔符鎮、六安縣焦家寨。

translations.literal: He then advanced and captured Fu garrison and Jiaojia Stockade in Lu'an County.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to take Fu garrison and Jiaojia Stockade in Lu'an County.

sentences.zh: 丁酉秋九月，由八柳渡河，入汴京。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn in dingyou he crossed the river at Baliu and entered Bianjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of dingyou he crossed at Baliu and entered Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 守臣劉甫置酒大慶殿。

translations.literal: The defending official Liu Fu set out wine in the Hall of Great Celebration.
translations.idiomatic: The commander Liu Fu prepared a banquet in the Hall of Great Celebration.

sentences.zh: 塔思曰：「此故金主所居，我人臣也，不可處此。」

translations.literal: Tarsi said: "This is where the former Jin sovereign once dwelt; I am but a subject — I cannot abide here."
translations.idiomatic: Tarsi said, "This was the Jin emperor's seat. I am only a subject — I cannot accept hospitality here."

sentences.zh: 遂宴於甫家。

translations.literal: He thereupon banqueted at Fu's home.
translations.idiomatic: He took the feast instead at Liu Fu's home.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，復與口溫不花攻光州，主將黃舜卿降。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he again with Kewen Buka attacked Guang Prefecture; the commander-in-chief Huang Shunqing surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he again joined Kewen Buka against Guang Prefecture, where the commander Huang Shunqing surrendered.

sentences.zh: 口溫不花別略黃州。

translations.literal: Kewen Buka separately reduced Huang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kewen Buka swept Huang Prefecture on a separate advance.

sentences.zh: 塔思攻大蘇山，斬首數千級，獲生口、牛馬以千數。

translations.literal: Tarsi attacked Dasu Mountain, beheading several thousand, and captured living captives and cattle and horses by the thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Tarsi stormed Dasu Mountain, killed several thousand men, and took thousands of captives and livestock.

sentences.zh: 戊戌春正月，至安慶府，官民皆遁於江東。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in wuxu he reached Anqing Prefecture; officials and commoners all fled east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of wuxu he reached Anqing, but officials and townspeople had already fled across the river to the east.

sentences.zh: 至北峽關，宋汪統制率兵三千降，遷之尉氏。

translations.literal: Reaching Beixia Pass, Song commander Wang led three thousand troops in surrender; he resettled them at Weishi.
translations.idiomatic: At Beixia Pass the Song commander Wang surrendered with three thousand men; Tarsi resettled them at Weishi.

sentences.zh: 三月，朝行在所。

translations.literal: In the third month he attended court at the mobile imperial residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he attended the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，帝宴群臣於行宮，塔思大醉。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn the Emperor banqueted the ministers at the traveling palace; Tarsi became greatly drunk.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, at a feast in the traveling palace, Tarsi drank himself into a stupor.

sentences.zh: 帝語侍臣曰：「塔思神已逝矣，其能久乎！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to attendants: "Tarsi's spirit has already departed — how long can he endure!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor murmured to his attendants, "Tarsi's soul has already left him. How much longer can he last?"

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，還雲中。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter he returned to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he returned to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 己亥春三月，薨，年二十八。

translations.literal: In the third month of spring in jihai he died; age twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third month of jihai, aged twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子碩篤兒幼，弟速渾察襲。

translations.literal: His son Shudur was young; his younger brother Suqunchar inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shudur was still a child, so his younger brother Suqunchar took the title.

sentences.zh: 碩篤兒既長，詔別賜民三千戶為食邑，得建國王旗幟，降五品印一、七品印二，付其家臣，置官屬如列侯故事。

translations.literal: When Shudur had grown, an edict separately granted three thousand households as a food fief; he was permitted to erect a prince's banners and standards; one seal of the fifth rank and two of the seventh rank were bestowed, given to his household retainers, and officials were appointed according to the precedent for enfeoffed lords.
