translations.idiomatic: When Shudur came of age, the court granted him three thousand tax households, royal banners, a fifth-rank and two seventh-rank seals for his household staff, and a full retinue like a feudal lord.

sentences.zh: 碩篤兒薨，子忽都華襲。

translations.literal: Shudur died; his son Khutua inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Shudur died, his son Khutua succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 忽都華薨，子忽都帖木兒襲。

translations.literal: Khutua died; his son Khudutemur inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Khutua died, his son Khudutemur succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 忽都帖木兒薨，子寶哥襲。

translations.literal: Khudutemur died; his son Baoge inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Khudutemur died, his son Baoge succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 寶哥薨，子道童襲。

translations.literal: Baoge died; his son Daotong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoge died, his son Daotong succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 速渾察，性嚴厲，賞罰明信，人莫敢犯。

translations.literal: Suqunchar by nature was stern and severe; rewards and punishments were clear and trusted; no one dared transgress.
translations.idiomatic: Suqunchar was stern by nature, his rewards and punishments unmistakable, and no one dared cross him.

sentences.zh: 與兄塔思從太宗攻鳳翔有功。

translations.literal: With his elder brother Tarsi he followed Emperor Taizong in attacking Fengxiang and achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Tarsi followed Emperor Taizong against Fengxiang and won distinction.

sentences.zh: 將兵抵潼關，與金人戰屢捷。

translations.literal: Leading troops to Tong Pass, he fought the Jin repeatedly with victory.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops to Tong Pass and won repeated victories over the Jin.

sentences.zh: 既滅金，皇子闊出攻宋棗陽，入郢，速渾察皆與焉。

translations.literal: After the Jin were destroyed, Imperial Prince Kuochu attacked Song Zaoyang and entered Ying; Suqunchar took part in all of it.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Jin he fought in Prince Kuochu's campaigns against Zaoyang and Ying.

sentences.zh: 歲己亥，塔思薨，速渾察襲爵，即上京之西阿兒查禿置營，總中都行省蒙古、漢軍。

translations.literal: In the year jihai, when Tarsi died, Suqunchar inherited the title; he immediately set camp west of Shangjing at Arqat and commanded the Mongol and Han armies of the Central Capital Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Tarsi died in jihai, Suqunchar inherited the title, established his camp at Arqat west of Shangjing, and took command of the Mongol and Han forces of the Central Capital Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 凡他行省監鎮事，必先白之，定其可否，而後上聞。

translations.literal: For all supervisory and garrison affairs in other branch secretariats, one had first to report to him, determine approval or rejection, and only then report upward.
translations.idiomatic: Every supervisory or garrison matter in the other branch secretariats had to be brought to him first for approval before it could be reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗遣使至，見其威容凜然，倜儻有奇氣，所部軍士紀綱整肅，還朝以告。

translations.literal: The Emperor once sent an envoy; seeing his imposing bearing, free and easy with a singular air, and the troops under his command disciplined and orderly, the envoy returned to court and reported.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial envoy who visited him reported back that he cut a formidable figure, carried himself with uncommon ease, and kept his troops in strict order.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「真木華黎家兒也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Truly a son of Muqali's house."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He is a true son of Muqali's house."

sentences.zh: 他國使有至者，每見皆倉皇失次，不能措辭，必慰撫良久，始得盡其所欲言。

translations.literal: When envoys from other states arrived, each time they met him they were flustered and lost composure, unable to arrange their words; he always had to comfort them at length before they could fully say what they wished.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign envoys who came before him were so unnerved they could barely speak; he always had to put them at ease at length before they could say what they had come to say.

sentences.zh: 左右或諫曰：「諸王百司既莫敢越，而復示之以威，使人怖畏，盍少加寬恕以待之。」

translations.literal: Attendants sometimes remonstrated: "The princes and all offices already dare not overstep; yet you again display severity and make men fearful — why not add a little leniency in receiving them?"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants sometimes urged him: "The princes and officials already dare not cross you. Why show such severity that envoys tremble before you? A little forbearance would serve better."

sentences.zh: 速渾察曰：「爾言誠是也，然時有不同，寬猛各有所宜施。

translations.literal: Suqunchar said: "Your words are indeed correct; yet times differ, and leniency and severity each have their proper application.
translations.idiomatic: Suqunchar replied, "You are right — but times differ, and leniency and severity each have their season.

sentences.zh: 天下初附，民心未安，萬一守者自縱，事變忽起，悔之晚矣。」

translations.literal: The realm has only just submitted; the people's hearts are not yet settled; if by any chance those who hold posts indulge themselves, sudden disturbances arise — then regret comes too late."
translations.idiomatic: The realm has only just submitted and the people are still unsettled. If local officials grow lax, trouble can erupt overnight — and then it will be too late for regret."

sentences.zh: 尋薨。

translations.literal: Soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died not long after.

sentences.zh: 延祐三年，贈宣忠同德翊運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封為東平郡王，謚忠宣。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanyou he was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister of Loyalty, Shared Virtue, and Support to the Dynasty, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master with the Privilege of an Imperial Chariot, and Pillar of the State; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping Commandery; temple name Zhongxuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 3 he was posthumously honored as Meritorious Minister of Loyalty, Shared Virtue, and Support to the Dynasty, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master with Imperial Chariot Privilege, and Pillar of the State, and enfeoffed posthumously as Prince of Dongping with the temple name Zhongxuan.

sentences.zh: 子四人：曰忽林池，襲王爵；

translations.literal: He had four sons: one named Hulinci, who inherited the princely title;
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Hulinci, who inherited the princely title;

sentences.zh: 曰乃燕；

translations.literal: one named Naiyan;
translations.idiomatic: Naiyan;

sentences.zh: 曰相威；

translations.literal: one named Xiangwei;
translations.idiomatic: Xiangwei;

sentences.zh: 曰撒蠻。

translations.literal: and one named Saman.
translations.idiomatic: and Saman.

sentences.zh: 相威自有傳。

translations.literal: Xiangwei has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangwei has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 乃燕，性謙和，好學，以賢能稱。

translations.literal: Naiyan by nature was modest and harmonious, loved learning, and was acclaimed for talent and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Naiyan was modest and gentle, devoted to learning, and widely praised for his ability.

sentences.zh: 速渾察既薨，憲宗擇於諸子，命乃燕襲爵。

translations.literal: After Suqunchar died, Emperor Möngke chose among the sons and ordered Naiyan to inherit the title.
translations.idiomatic: After Suqunchar's death, Emperor Möngke chose Naiyan from among the sons to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 乃燕力辭曰：「臣有兄忽林池當襲。」

translations.literal: Naiyan forcefully declined, saying: "I have an elder brother, Hulinci, who ought to inherit."
translations.idiomatic: Naiyan refused firmly: "My elder brother Hulinci is the rightful heir."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕知之，然柔弱不能勝。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I know it, yet he is too weak and cannot prevail."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I know — but he is too soft for the burden."

sentences.zh: 忽林池亦固讓，乃燕頓首涕泣力辭，不得命，既而曰：「若然，則王爵必不敢受，願代臣兄行軍國之事。」

translations.literal: Hulinci also firmly yielded; Naiyan bowed his head, wept, and forcefully declined but could not obtain permission; then he said: "If so, I dare not accept the princely title; I wish to act in my brother's stead in military and state affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Hulinci refused as well. Naiyan kowtowed and wept but could not change the order. At last he said, "Then I dare not take the title myself. Let me manage military and state affairs in my brother's name."

sentences.zh: 於是忽林池襲為國王，事無巨細，必與乃燕謀議，剖決精當，無所擁滯。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hulinci inherited as king; matters great and small were always deliberated with Naiyan; decisions were precise and apt, with nothing blocked or delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Hulinci took the kingship, and on every matter, large or small, he consulted Naiyan. Their decisions were sharp and nothing piled up unresolved.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛藩，常與論事。

translations.literal: When Kublai was in his princely domain, he often discussed affairs with him.
translations.idiomatic: While Kublai was still heir apparent, he often sought Naiyan's counsel.

sentences.zh: 乃燕敷陳大義，又明習典故。

translations.literal: Naiyan set forth great principles and was moreover well versed in historical precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Naiyan spoke with moral clarity and knew the classics and precedents well.

sentences.zh: 世祖謂左右曰：「乃燕後必可大用。」

translations.literal: Kublai said to those beside him: "Naiyan in future can surely be greatly employed."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai told his attendants, "Naiyan will be of great use one day."

sentences.zh: 因號之曰薛禪，猶華言大賢也。

translations.literal: He thereupon styled him Setsen — as the Chinese say, "great sage."
translations.idiomatic: He gave him the name Setsen — "great sage" in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 乃燕雖居顯要，而小心謹畏，每誨群從子弟曰：「先世從太祖皇帝出入矢石間，被堅執銳，斬將搴旗，勤勞四十餘年，遂成功名。

translations.literal: Though Naiyan held a prominent post, he was cautious and reverent; he often admonished the younger kinsmen, saying: "Our forebears followed Genghis Khan in and out among arrows and stones, donned armor and grasped sharp weapons, beheaded generals and seized banners, toiled more than forty years, and thus achieved fame and merit.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held high office, Naiyan remained careful and restrained. He often warned the younger kinsmen: "Our forebears followed Genghis Khan through arrow and stone fire, armored and armed, taking enemy banners and generals' heads, laboring more than forty years to win the fame we enjoy.

sentences.zh: 以故一家蒙恩深厚，可謂極矣。

translations.literal: For this reason one family has received grace deep and profound — it may be called the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Our house has received imperial favor beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 慎勿驕惰，以墮先王之名，爾曹戒之。」

translations.literal: Take care not to grow proud and lazy, lest you fall from the name of our forefathers — you must all take warning."
translations.idiomatic: Do not grow proud or slack and stain the name our forefathers won. Take this to heart."

sentences.zh: 病卒。

translations.literal: He died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness.

sentences.zh: 世祖聞之，為之悲悼。

translations.literal: When Kublai heard of it, he grieved and mourned for him.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai grieved deeply when he heard the news.

sentences.zh: 至正八年，贈中奉大夫、遼陽等處行中書省參知政事、護軍，追封魯郡公。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhizheng he was posthumously granted Grand Master for Faithful Service, Assistant Administrator of the Branch Secretariat of Liaoyang and other places, and Defender of the Army; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 8 he was posthumously honored as Grand Master for Faithful Service, Assistant Administrator of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, and Defender of the Army, and enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 子二人：曰碩德，曰伯顏察兒。

translations.literal: He had two sons: one named Shude, one named Bayancha'er.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Shude and Bayancha'er.

sentences.zh: 霸突魯，從世祖征伐，為先鋒元帥，累立戰功。

translations.literal: Baturlu followed Kublai on campaigns, served as vanguard marshal, and repeatedly achieved military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Baturlu campaigned with Kublai as vanguard marshal and won repeated honors in battle.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛邸，從容語霸突魯曰：「今天下稍定，我欲勸主上駐驛回鶻，以休兵息民，何如？」

translations.literal: When Kublai was in his princely residence, he spoke at ease to Baturlu, saying: "Now the realm is somewhat settled; I wish to urge the sovereign to halt the imperial progress in Qocho and rest the troops and soothe the people — what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: While still heir apparent, Kublai once said to Baturlu, "The realm is settling down. I mean to urge the khan to halt the court at Qocho and give the armies and people rest. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「幽燕之地，龍蟠虎踞，形勢雄偉，南控江淮，北連朔漠。

translations.literal: He replied: "The lands of You and Yan — coiled like a dragon, crouched like a tiger — are imposing in terrain; south they control the Jiang and Huai, north they connect to the northern deserts.
translations.idiomatic: Baturlu answered, "You and Yan lie like a dragon coiled and a tiger crouched — a commanding terrain. They hold the Jiang and Huai to the south and reach the northern steppe.

sentences.zh: 且天子必居中以受四方朝覲。

translations.literal: Moreover the Son of Heaven must dwell at the center to receive homage from the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: A Son of Heaven must sit at the center to receive tribute from every direction.

sentences.zh: 大王果欲經營天下，駐驛之所，非燕不可。」

translations.literal: If Your Highness truly wishes to manage the realm, the place to halt the imperial progress cannot be other than Yan."
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to rule the realm, Your Highness, there is no place to fix the court but Yan."

sentences.zh: 世祖憮然曰：「非卿言，我幾失之。」

translations.literal: Kublai, startled, said: "Had it not been for your words, I would nearly have missed it."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said with a start, "Without your counsel I would have missed the mark."

sentences.zh: 己未秋，命霸突魯率諸軍由蔡伐宋，且移檄諭宋沿邊諸將，遂與世祖兵合而南，五戰皆捷，遂渡大江，傅於鄂。

translations.literal: In the autumn of jiwei he ordered Baturlu to lead the armies from Cai to attack Song, and also issued a proclamation informing Song border generals; he then joined Kublai's forces and marched south; five battles were all victorious; they crossed the Great River and pressed close to E.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of jiwei he ordered Baturlu to lead the armies from Cai against Song and sent proclamations to the Song border commanders. He joined Kublai's force marching south, won five battles in succession, crossed the Yangzi, and closed on Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 會憲宗崩於蜀，阿裏不哥構亂和林，世祖北還，留霸突魯總軍務，以待命。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Möngke died in Shu; Ariq Böke raised rebellion at Karakorum; Kublai returned north and left Baturlu in overall command of military affairs, awaiting orders.
translations.idiomatic: Then Möngke died in Sichuan and Ariq Böke rebelled at Karakorum. Kublai withdrew north and left Baturlu in command of the army, awaiting further orders.

sentences.zh: 世祖至開平，即位，還定都於燕。

translations.literal: Kublai reached Kaiping, ascended the throne, and returned to fix the capital at Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai reached Kaiping, took the throne, and made Yan his capital.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「朕居此以臨天下，霸突魯之力也。」

translations.literal: He once said: "That I dwell here to oversee the realm is Baturlu's doing."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "I rule the realm from here because of Baturlu."

sentences.zh: 師還，中統二年卒於軍。

translations.literal: When the army returned, in the second year of Zhongtong he died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he died in camp in Zhongtong 2.

sentences.zh: 大德八年，追贈推誠宣力翊衛功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、東平王，謚武靖。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dade he was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister of Sincere Devotion, Proclaimed Strength, and Support and Guard, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master with the Privilege of an Imperial Chariot, Pillar of the State, and Prince of Dongping; temple name Wujing.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 8 he was posthumously honored as Meritorious Minister of Sincere Devotion, Proclaimed Strength, and Support and Guard, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master with Imperial Chariot Privilege, Pillar of the State, and Prince of Dongping, with the temple name Wujing.

sentences.zh: 夫人帖木倫，昭睿順聖皇后同母兄也。

translations.literal: His wife was Temülün; he was the elder uterine brother of Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was Lady Temülün. He was the elder uterine brother of Empress Chabi (Zhaorui Shunsheng).

sentences.zh: 子四人：長安童，次定童，次霸都虎臺；

translations.literal: He had four sons: the eldest Antong, next Dingtong, next Badu Qutai;
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Antong, Dingtong, and Badu Qutai;

sentences.zh: 他姬子曰和童，襲國王。

translations.literal: a son by another consort named Hetong inherited the kingship.
translations.idiomatic: and Hetong, a son by a secondary wife, who inherited the kingship.

sentences.zh: 安童別有傳。

translations.literal: Antong has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Antong has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 只必，幼嗜讀書，習翰墨。

translations.literal: Zhibi from youth loved reading and practiced brush and ink.
translations.idiomatic: Zhibi loved books from childhood and trained in letters.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年監東平，官少中大夫，多善政，以清白稱。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan he supervised Dongping, holding the office of Junior Grand Master of the Palace; he had many good policies and was acclaimed for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 14 he supervised Dongping as Junior Grand Master of the Palace, governing well and earning a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 嘗出家藏書二千餘卷，置東平廟學，使學徒講肄之。

translations.literal: He once brought out more than two thousand volumes from his family collection, placed them in the Dongping temple school, and had students lecture and study them.
translations.idiomatic: He donated more than two thousand volumes from his family library to the Dongping temple school for students to study.

sentences.zh: 尋授嘉議大夫、江南湖北道提刑按察使，改浙西。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Counsel and Intendant and Surveillance Commissioner of the Jiangnan Huguang Circuit, then transferred to Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Master for Splendid Counsel and Surveillance Commissioner for Jiangnan Huguang, then transferred to Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 大德四年入覲，賜金段十匹。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dade he came to court for audience and was granted ten bolts of gold brocade.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 4 he attended court and received ten bolts of gold brocade.

sentences.zh: 明年春卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: The next spring he died; age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following spring, aged fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 子三人，皆早喪。

translations.literal: He had three sons; all died young.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons, all of whom died young.

sentences.zh: 自只必除按察使，弟禿不申嗣其職。

translations.literal: From the time Zhibi was appointed surveillance commissioner, his younger brother Tubushen succeeded to the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhibi became surveillance commissioner, his younger brother Tubushen succeeded him in the office.

sentences.zh: 禿不申，性淳靖，喜怒不形，知民疾苦，而能以善道之。

translations.literal: Tubushen by nature was pure and tranquil; joy and anger did not show on his face; he knew the people's hardships and could guide them by good means.
translations.idiomatic: Tubushen was plain and steady, never showing anger or pleasure on his face. He understood the people's hardships and knew how to lead them well.

sentences.zh: 旱嘗致禱，即雨。

translations.literal: During drought he once offered prayers, and rain immediately came.
translations.idiomatic: Once during a drought he prayed, and rain followed at once.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，請於朝，發廩以賑之。

translations.literal: In years of famine he petitioned the court and opened granaries to relieve the people.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years he petitioned the court to open the granaries for relief.

sentences.zh: 睦同僚，興學校。

translations.literal: He harmonized with colleagues and promoted schools.
translations.idiomatic: He kept peace among his colleagues and promoted schools.

sentences.zh: 加太中大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 士民刻石，紀其政績云。

translations.literal: Gentry and commoners carved stone to record his administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Local gentry and townspeople set up a stone inscription recording his achievements.

sentences.zh: 卒年五十一。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 子五人：長不老赤，次塔實脫因，次阿魯灰，次完者不花，次留住馬。

translations.literal: He had five sons: the eldest Bulagchi, next Tashidetin, next Arughui, next Ojanbuqa, and the youngest Liuzhuma.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: Bulagchi, Tashidetin, Arughui, Ojanbuqa, and Liuzhuma.

sentences.zh: 皆以次嗣為東平達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Each in turn succeeded as darughachi of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Each in turn succeeded as darughachi of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 脫脫，祖嗣國王速渾察，沈深有智略。

translations.literal: Tuotuo — his grandfather Suqunchar, who succeeded as king, was deep and reserved, with wisdom and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo's grandfather Suqunchar, who had succeeded to the kingship, was grave and thoughtful, possessed of wisdom and strategic skill.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉命征討，所向克捷。

translations.literal: Once ordered on campaigns of suppression, wherever he went he achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: When sent on campaign, he won wherever he marched.

sentences.zh: 父撒蠻，幼穎異，自繈褓時，世祖撫育之若子。

translations.literal: His father Saman, while young was precocious and exceptional; from swaddling clothes the Shizu raised and nurtured him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: His father Saman was unusually gifted even as a child; from infancy Kublai Khan had raised and cared for him as though he were his own son.

sentences.zh: 嘗挾之南征，同舟濟大江，慮其有失，系之禦榻。

translations.literal: Once he took him along on a southern campaign; in the same boat they crossed the great river; fearing he might be lost, he tied him to the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: On one southern campaign he brought the boy along; crossing the great river in the same boat, he tied him to the imperial couch lest he be lost overboard.

sentences.zh: 及長，常侍左右。

translations.literal: When grown, he constantly attended at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Once he came of age, he was constantly at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗詔之曰：「男女異路，古制也，況掖庭乎。

translations.literal: The Emperor once instructed him, saying: "Men and women keep separate paths — it is an ancient regulation; how much more so in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told him, "Men and women must keep to separate paths — that is ancient law, and all the more so within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 禮不可不肅，汝其司之。」

translations.literal: Rites must not lack dignity; you shall oversee this."
translations.idiomatic: Decorum must be strictly maintained. You are to enforce it."

sentences.zh: 既而近臣孛羅銜命遽出，行失其次。

translations.literal: Soon after, the close attendant Boluo received orders and hastened out, his conduct falling out of proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a close attendant named Boluo, carrying orders, rushed out in violation of the proper sequence.

sentences.zh: 撒蠻怒其違禮，執而囚之別室。

translations.literal: Saman, angered at this breach of ritual, seized him and imprisoned him in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: Saman, furious at this breach of protocol, seized him and confined him in a separate room.

sentences.zh: 帝怪其久不至，詢知其故，命釋其罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor wondered at his long absence, inquired and learned the reason, and ordered his crime released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wondered why Boluo had not returned and, on learning what had happened, ordered him released.

sentences.zh: 撒蠻因進曰：「令自陛下出，陛下乃自違之，何以責臣下乎？」

translations.literal: Saman then advanced and said: "The order came from Your Majesty; Your Majesty now violates it yourself — how can you hold subordinates accountable?"
translations.idiomatic: Saman then stepped forward and said, "The rule came from Your Majesty, yet Your Majesty now breaks it yourself — how can you hold your officials accountable?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言誠是也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What you say is indeed correct."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "What you say is quite right."

sentences.zh: 由是有意大任之。

translations.literal: From this he intended to grant him great responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on he meant to entrust Saman with weighty duties.

sentences.zh: 會以疾卒，不果，年僅一十有七。

translations.literal: But he died of illness — it did not come to pass; he was only seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: But Saman died of illness before this could happen; he was only seventeen.

sentences.zh: 脫脫幼既失怙，其母孛羅海篤意教之，孜孜若恐不及。

translations.literal: Tuotuo, having lost his father while young, his mother Boroqai earnestly taught him, diligently as if fearing she could not keep up.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo lost his father while still a boy; his mother Boroqai devoted herself to his education, teaching him tirelessly as though she could never do enough.

sentences.zh: 稍長，直宿衛，世祖復親誨導，尤以嗜酒為戒。

translations.literal: When somewhat grown he served on palace guard duty; the Shizu again personally instructed him, especially warning against fondness for wine.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he entered palace guard service, and Kublai again tutored him in person, above all warning him against drunkenness.

sentences.zh: 既冠，儀觀甚偉。

translations.literal: Having reached manhood, his bearing and appearance were very imposing.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age his presence was strikingly handsome and imposing.

sentences.zh: 喜與儒士語，每聞一善言善行，若獲拱璧，終身識之不忘。

translations.literal: He delighted in conversing with Confucian scholars; whenever he heard one good word or good deed, it was as if he had obtained a ritual jade disc; he remembered it all his life without forgetting.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to talk with Confucian scholars; every worthy word or deed he heard he treasured like a ceremonial jade, and never forgot it as long as he lived.

sentences.zh: 至元二十四年，從征乃顏。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Zhiyuan, he followed the campaign against Nayan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of the Zhiyuan era he took part in the campaign against Prince Nayan.

sentences.zh: 帝駐驛於山巔，旌旗蔽野。

translations.literal: The Emperor halted at a relay station on the mountain peak; banners and flags covered the wild.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor encamped at a post station on a mountain summit; banners and standards blanketed the countryside.

sentences.zh: 鼓未作，候者報有隙可乘，脫脫即擐甲率家奴數十人疾馳擊之。

translations.literal: Before the drums sounded, scouts reported a gap to exploit; Tuotuo immediately donned armor, led several dozen household slaves, and galloped swiftly to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Before the drums had even sounded, scouts reported an opening; Tuotuo at once donned armor, led several dozen household retainers, and charged.

sentences.zh: 眾皆披靡不敢前。

translations.literal: The masses all scattered and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy ranks broke and none dared press forward.

sentences.zh: 帝望見之，大加嗟賞，遣使者勞之，且召還曰：「卿勿輕進，此寇易擒也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor saw him from afar and greatly praised him, sent an envoy to console him, and also summoned him back, saying: "Do not press lightly forward — these bandits are easy to capture."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw him from afar and was deeply impressed; he sent an envoy to commend him and recalled him, saying, "Do not advance rashly — these rebels are easily taken."

sentences.zh: 視其刀已折，馬已中箭矣。

translations.literal: Seeing his saber already broken and his horse already struck by arrows.
translations.idiomatic: He saw that Tuotuo's blade was broken and his horse had already been hit by arrows.

sentences.zh: 帝顧謂近臣曰：「撒蠻不幸早死，脫脫幼，朕撫而教之，常恐其不立，今能如此，撒蠻可謂有子矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor turned to close attendants and said: "Saman unfortunately died early; Tuotuo is young; I raised and taught him, always fearing he would not establish himself; now he can do this — Saman may be said to have a son."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to his attendants and said, "Saman died young, and Tuotuo is still a boy. I raised and taught him, always fearing he would not amount to anything — yet now he has shown himself like this. Saman may be said to have left a worthy son."

sentences.zh: 遂親解佩刀及所乘馬賜之。

translations.literal: He then personally unfastened his girdle-sword and the horse he rode and bestowed them on him.
translations.idiomatic: He then personally removed his own belt-sword and the horse he was riding and gave them to Tuotuo.

sentences.zh: 由是深加器重，得預聞機密之事。

translations.literal: From this he deeply increased his trust and esteem, and was permitted to hear confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the emperor placed great trust in him and admitted him to confidential deliberations.

sentences.zh: 其後哈丹復為亂，成宗時在潛邸，督師往征之。

translations.literal: Afterwards Khadan rebelled again; when Chengzong was in the Hidden Residence he supervised the army to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Khadan rebelled again, Chengzong — then still heir apparent — took command of the army sent to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 脫脫引眾率先躍馬蹙之，其眾大潰。

translations.literal: Tuotuo led the troops, first leaping his horse to press them; their masses greatly routed.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo led the vanguard, spurring his horse forward to close on the enemy, and put their forces to rout.

sentences.zh: 脫脫馬陷於淖泥中，哈丹兵復進挑戰，脫脫弟阿老瓦丁奮戈沖擊，遂大敗之。

translations.literal: Tuotuo's horse sank in mire; Khadan's troops again advanced to challenge; Tuotuo's younger brother Alawadin wielded his spear and charged; they thereupon greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuotuo's horse sank into boggy mud, Khadan's troops pressed the attack; Tuotuo's younger brother Alawadin charged with his halberd and drove them to a great defeat.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，其寵顧為尤篤，常侍禁闥，出入惟謹，退語家人曰：「我昔親承先帝訓，飭令毋嗜飲，今未能絕也。

translations.literal: When Chengzong acceded, his favor and regard were especially deep; he constantly attended within the forbidden gates; entering and leaving with sole care; retiring he told his family: "I formerly received the former Emperor's instruction in person, charging me not to indulge in drink; I have not yet been able to quit entirely.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong took the throne, his favor toward Tuotuo was especially warm; Tuotuo served constantly within the inner palace, ever cautious in coming and going. In private he told his household, "I once received the late emperor's instruction never to indulge in wine, yet I still have not broken the habit entirely.

sentences.zh: 豈有為人知過而不能改者乎！

translations.literal: How can there be one who knows his fault yet cannot reform!
translations.idiomatic: Can a man who knows his fault yet fail to mend it?

sentences.zh: 自今以往，家人有以酒至吾前者，即痛懲之。」

translations.literal: From now on, if any family member brings wine before me, severely punish them."
translations.idiomatic: From this day forward, if anyone in my household brings wine into my presence, punish him severely."

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，喜曰：「紥剌兒臺如脫脫者無幾，今能剛制於酒，真可大用矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and said with joy: "Among the Jalair there are few like Tuotuo; now able to sternly restrain himself in wine — truly fit for great employment."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this he said with delight, "Among the Jalair there are few men like Tuotuo. That he can now master his taste for wine shows he is truly fit for high office."

sentences.zh: 即拜資德大夫、上都留守、通政院使、虎賁衛親軍都指揮使，政令嚴肅，克修其職。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed Grand Master for Promotion of Virtue, Uplands Keeper, Commissioner of the Bureau of Transmission, and Commander-in-Chief of the Imperial Bodyguard of the Tiger Garrison; his commands were stern and he fully performed his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo was at once appointed Grand Master for Promotion of Virtue, Keeper of the Upper Capital, Commissioner of the Bureau of Transmission, and Commander-in-Chief of the Tiger Garrison Imperial Guard. His orders were strict and he discharged every duty.

sentences.zh: 三年，朝議以江浙行省地大人眾，非世臣有重望者，不足以鎮之。

translations.literal: In the third year, court discussion held that the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat's territory was large and its population numerous; unless a hereditary minister of great renown, one was insufficient to pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of his reign the court decided that the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat was too vast and populous to be governed by anyone less than a hereditary minister of the highest standing.

sentences.zh: 進拜榮祿大夫、江浙等處行中書省平章政事，有旨，命中書祖道都門外以餞之。

translations.literal: Promoted to Grand Master for Glorious Emolument and Pingzhang of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat; an edict ordered the Central Secretariat to perform the road-leaving ceremony outside the capital gate to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master for Glorious Emolument and Pingzhang of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat, and the emperor ordered the Central Secretariat to hold a farewell ceremony for him outside the capital gate.

sentences.zh: 始至，嚴飭左右，毋預公家事，且戒其掾屬曰：「仆從有私囑者，慎勿聽。

translations.literal: Upon first arriving he strictly ordered those around him not to interfere in public office affairs, and warned his clerks: "If attendants bring private requests, take care not to heed them.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he arrived he strictly forbade his staff to meddle in official business on others' behalf, and warned his secretaries, "If any servant brings a private request, do not listen.

sentences.zh: 若軍民諸事，有關於利害者，則言之。

translations.literal: If military and civilian affairs touch on benefit and harm, then speak of them.
translations.idiomatic: But if any matter affecting soldiers or civilians, for good or ill, comes to your attention, speak of it.

sentences.zh: 當言而不言，爾之責也；

translations.literal: When you should speak but do not speak, that is your fault;
translations.idiomatic: If you should speak and do not, that is your fault;

sentences.zh: 言而不聽，我之咎也。」

translations.literal: when you speak but I do not heed, that is my fault."
translations.idiomatic: if you speak and I do not listen, that is mine."

sentences.zh: 聞者為之悚栗。

translations.literal: Those who heard were awed and trembling.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard him were shaken with awe.

sentences.zh: 時朱清、張瑄以海運之故，致位參知政事，恃其勢位，多行不法，恐事覺，以黃金五十兩、珠三囊賂脫脫，求蔽其罪。

translations.literal: At the time Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan, because of sea transport, had risen to Vice Grand Councillor; relying on their power and position they often acted unlawfully; fearing exposure they bribed Tuotuo with fifty taels of gold and three bags of pearls, seeking to conceal their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qing and Zhang Xuan had risen to vice grand councillor on the strength of the sea-transport monopoly; abusing their power they committed many illegal acts, and fearing discovery they offered Tuotuo fifty taels of gold and three bags of pearls to cover their crimes.

sentences.zh: 脫脫大怒，系之有司，遣使者以聞。

translations.literal: Tuotuo flew into great anger, bound them over to the authorities, and sent an envoy to report.
translations.idiomatic: Tuotuo was furious; he had them arrested and handed over to the courts, then reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝喜曰：「脫脫我家老臣之子孫，其志固宜與眾人殊。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said with joy: "Tuotuo, descendant of our family's old minister — his will should indeed differ from the common run."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with pleasure, "Tuotuo is the descendant of a long-serving minister of our house — it is only fitting that his integrity should set him apart from ordinary men."

sentences.zh: 賜內府黃金五十兩，命回使寵賚之。

translations.literal: Granted fifty taels of gold from the inner treasury; ordered the returning envoy to confer honors on him.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with fifty taels of gold from the palace treasury, and the returning envoy was ordered to convey the imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 有豪民白晝殺人者，脫脫立命有司按法誅之，自是豪猾屏息，民賴以安。

translations.literal: When a powerful commoner killed someone in broad daylight, Tuotuo immediately ordered the authorities to execute him according to law; from this the bold and unruly held their breath, and the people relied on this for peace.
translations.idiomatic: When a local bully murdered a man in broad daylight, Tuotuo ordered him executed at once by due process of law; thereafter the violent and lawless fell silent, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 帝以浙民相安之久，未及召還，大德十一年，卒於位，年四十四。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because the Zhejiang people had long been at peace under him, had not yet summoned him back; in the eleventh year of Dade he died in office, age forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Because the people of Zhejiang had prospered under his rule, the emperor had not yet recalled him; in the eleventh year of the Dade era he died in office at the age of forty-four.

sentences.zh: 子朵兒只，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Dorji has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dorji is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: ○博爾術

translations.literal: ○ Bo'orchu
translations.idiomatic: Bo'orchu

sentences.zh: 博爾術，阿兒剌氏。

translations.literal: Bo'orchu, of the Arlat clan.
translations.idiomatic: Bo'orchu belonged to the Arlat clan.

sentences.zh: 始祖孛端察兒，以才武雄朔方。

translations.literal: The founding ancestor Borte Chino, through talent and martial prowess dominated the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The clan's founding ancestor Borte Chino had made himself a power in the north through talent and arms.

sentences.zh: 父納忽阿兒闌，與烈祖神元皇帝接境，敦睦鄰好。

translations.literal: His father Naghu Arlan, bordering the Liezu Shenyuan Emperor's domain, maintained neighborly friendship.
translations.idiomatic: His father Naghu Arlan lived on the border of the domain of the Liezu Shenyuan Emperor and kept cordial relations with his neighbors.

sentences.zh: 博爾術誌意沈雄，善戰知兵，事太祖於潛邸，共履艱危，義均同氣，征伐四出，無往不從。

translations.literal: Bo'orchu was resolute in purpose, deep and bold, skilled in battle and knowing warfare; he served the Taizu at the Hidden Residence, together treading hardship and peril, righteousness equal to blood kin; campaigns went out on four sides — nowhere he did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Bo'orchu was steadfast and formidable, skilled in war and versed in military affairs. He served Genghis Khan in his years of struggle, sharing every hardship as though they were brothers by blood; on campaign after campaign he was always at the khan's side.

sentences.zh: 時諸部未寧，博爾術每警夜，帝寢必安枕。

translations.literal: When the various tribes were not yet pacified, Bo'orchu every night kept watch; the Emperor slept secure on his pillow.
translations.idiomatic: While the tribes were still unsettled, Bo'orchu stood guard every night so that the khan could sleep in peace.

sentences.zh: 寓直於內，語及政要，或至達旦。

translations.literal: Dwelling on duty within the palace, when talk touched on key policy, sometimes until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: On duty within the palace, he and the khan would discuss affairs of state until dawn.

sentences.zh: 君臣之契，猶魚水也。

translations.literal: The bond between ruler and minister was like fish and water.
translations.idiomatic: The bond between lord and minister was like fish and water.

sentences.zh: 初，要兒斤部卒盜牧馬，博爾術與往追之，時年十三，知眾寡不敵，乃出奇從旁夾擊之，盜舍所掠去。

translations.literal: Initially, a soldier of the Yirkin tribe stole grazing horses; Bo'orchu went with others to pursue; at age thirteen, knowing they were outnumbered, he devised a surprise flank attack; the bandits abandoned what they had seized and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when a Yirkin tribesman stole horses from the herd, Bo'orchu joined the pursuit. He was only thirteen, but seeing they were outnumbered he launched a flanking attack by surprise; the thieves dropped their loot and fled.

sentences.zh: 即戰於大赤兀裏，兩軍相接，下令殊死戰，跬步勿退。

translations.literal: They immediately fought at Da Chi'wuli; the two armies met; he ordered fight to the death, not one step retreat.
translations.idiomatic: They fought at once at Da Chi'wuli. As the two forces clashed he ordered a fight to the death — not one step back.

sentences.zh: 博爾術系馬於腰，跽而引滿，分寸不離故處，太祖嘉其勇膽。

translations.literal: Bo'orchu tied his horse at his waist, knelt and drew the bow to full draw, not one inch from his original position; the Taizu praised his courageous boldness.
translations.idiomatic: Bo'orchu tethered his horse to his belt, knelt, and drew his bow to the full, never shifting a foot from his post; Genghis Khan praised his courage.

sentences.zh: 又嘗潰圍於怯列，太祖失馬，博爾術擁帝累騎餌馳，頓止中野。

translations.literal: Also once broke through encirclement at Qilie; the Taizu lost his horse; Bo'orchu shielded the Emperor, riding relay horses with forage at a gallop, halting in the open wild.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, when they broke out of an encirclement at Qilie, the khan lost his mount; Bo'orchu shielded him, changing horses in relays at a gallop until they halted in the open country.

sentences.zh: 會天雨雪，失牙帳所在，臥草澤中，與木華黎張氈裘以蔽帝，同夕植立，足跡不移，及旦，雪深數尺，遂免於難。

translations.literal: Then heaven snowed and rained; they lost where the yurt was; lying in marsh grass, with Muqali they spread felt cloaks to screen the Emperor; the same evening they stood planted, footprints unmoved; by dawn snow was several feet deep; thus they escaped disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Snow began to fall and they lost track of the camp. Lying in the marsh grass, Bo'orchu and Muqali spread felt cloaks to shelter the khan; all night they stood in place without shifting their feet, and by dawn the snow lay several feet deep — thus they escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 篾裏期之戰，亦以風雪迷陣，再入敵中，求太祖不見，急趨輜重，則帝已還臥憩車中，聞博爾術至，曰：「聰天贊我也。」

translations.literal: At the battle of Merkit, again wind and snow obscured the formation; entering the enemy a second time, seeking the Taizu and not seeing him, he hurried toward the baggage train — the Emperor had already returned to lie resting in the carriage; hearing Bo'orchu had arrived, said: "Heaven with clear wisdom aids me."
translations.idiomatic: At the battle against the Merkits, wind and snow again blinded the field. Bo'orchu plunged back into the enemy ranks searching for the khan; not finding him, he raced toward the baggage train — the khan was already resting in his carriage. When he heard Bo'orchu had come, he said, "Heaven itself has sent him to aid me."

sentences.zh: 丙寅歲，太祖即皇帝位，君臣之分益密，嘗從容謂博爾術及木華黎曰：「今國內平定，多汝等之力，我之與汝，猶車之有轅，身之有臂，汝等宜體此勿替。」

translations.literal: In the bingyin year the Taizu assumed the imperial throne; the distinction between ruler and minister grew closer; he once leisurely said to Bo'orchu and Muqali: "Now the realm within is pacified — much through your power; my relation to you is like a cart having its yoke-bar, a body having its arms — you should embody this and not fall short."
translations.idiomatic: In the bingyin year Genghis Khan took the imperial throne, and the bond between ruler and minister grew closer still. He once said calmly to Bo'orchu and Muqali, "The realm is now at peace — largely through your efforts. You are to me what the yoke-bar is to a cart, what the arms are to a body — hold to that and never fall short."

sentences.zh: 遂以博爾術及木華黎為左右萬戶，各以其屬翊衛，位在諸將上。

translations.literal: He then made Bo'orchu and Muqali Left and Right Myriarchs, each with their followers as attendant guard, rank above all generals.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Bo'orchu and Muqali the Left and Right Myriarchs, each commanding his own followers as a personal guard, with rank above all other commanders.

sentences.zh: 皇鬃察哈歹出鎮西域，有旨從博爾術受教，博爾術教以人生經涉險阻，必獲善地，她過無輕舍止。

translations.literal: Imperial Prince Zongchahadai went out to garrison the Western Regions; an edict ordered him to receive instruction from Bo'orchu; Bo'orchu taught that in life when traversing peril and obstruction one must gain good ground; when passing through do not lightly halt and camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Imperial Prince Zongchahadai was sent to govern the Western Regions, an edict directed him to learn from Bo'orchu. Bo'orchu taught him that in a life of hardship one must secure good ground and never lightly halt along the way.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂皇子曰：「朕之教汝，亦不逾是。」

translations.literal: The Taizu told the imperial princes: "My instruction to you also does not exceed this."
translations.idiomatic: Genghis Khan told his sons, "What I teach you goes no further than this."

sentences.zh: 未幾，賜廣平路戶一亡七千三百有奇為分地。

translations.literal: Not long afterward Bo'orchu was granted more than seventeen thousand three hundred registered households in Guangping Circuit as his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward Bo'orchu was granted more than seventeen thousand three hundred registered households in Guangping Circuit as his fief.

sentences.zh: 以老病薨，太祖痛悼之。

translations.literal: He died of old age and illness; the Taizu grieved deeply.
translations.idiomatic: He died of old age and illness, and Genghis Khan mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 大德五年，贈推忠協謀佐運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司，追封廣平王，謚武忠。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dade, posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Pushed Loyalty, Conspired in Counsel, and Assisted the Dynasty, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master of the Palace with the same ceremonies as the Three Ducal Ministers; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Guangping; posthumous name Wuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Dade era he was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister of Loyal Counsel and Dynastic Service, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Master of the Palace with honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Guangping with the posthumous name Wuzhong.

sentences.zh: 子孛欒臺，襲爵萬戶，贈推誠宣力保順功臣、太師、開府儀同三司，追封圭平王，謚忠定。

translations.literal: His son Bolotai inherited the myriarchy; posthumously granted Meritorious Minister Who Pushed Sincerity, Deployed Strength, and Preserved Obedience, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master of the Palace with the same ceremonies as the Three Ducal Ministers; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Guiping; posthumous name Zhongding.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bolotai inherited the myriarchy and was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister of Sincere Service and Loyal Strength, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Master of the Palace with honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Guiping with the posthumous name Zhongding.

sentences.zh: 孫玉昔帖木兒。

translations.literal: His grandson Usutai Temür.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson was Usutai Temür.

sentences.zh: 玉昔帖木兒，世祖時嘗寵以不名，賜號月呂魯那演，猶華言能官也。

translations.literal: Usutai Temür — in Shizu times was once favored by not using his name; granted the title Yebulun Nayin, meaning in Chinese "capable official."
translations.idiomatic: In Kublai Khan's reign Usutai Temür was so favored that the emperor addressed him by title rather than by name, granting him the style Yebulun Nayin — "capable minister" in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 弱冠襲爵，統按臺部眾，器量宏達，莫測其際。

translations.literal: At weak-crown he inherited the title, commanded the Aitai tribesmen; his capacity broad and far-reaching, none could fathom its bounds.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title while still young and took command of the Aitai tribesmen; his breadth of mind was so great that none could measure it.

sentences.zh: 世祖聞其賢，驛召赴闕，見其風骨龐乎，解御服銀貂賜之。

translations.literal: The Shizu heard of his worth, summoned him post-haste to court; seeing his bearing majestic, removed his own imperial garment of silver sable and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai, hearing of his merit, summoned him urgently to court; struck by his imposing presence, the emperor removed his own silver-sable court robe and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 時重太官內膳之選，特命領其事。

translations.literal: At the time the selection of Grand Provisioner's inner pantry was heavily regarded; he was specially ordered to head that office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the post overseeing the imperial kitchen was held in high regard, and he was specially appointed to it.

sentences.zh: 侍宴內殿，玉昔帖木兒起性酒，詔諸王妃皆為答禮。

translations.literal: Attending a banquet in the inner hall, Usutai Temür proposed a toast; an edict ordered all imperial princesses-consort to return the courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet in the inner hall Usutai Temür offered a toast, and an edict commanded every imperial consort to return the courtesy.

sentences.zh: 至元十二年，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhiyuan, appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of the Zhiyuan era he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時江南既定，益封功臣後，遂賜全州清湘縣戶為分地。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan had been settled, further enfeoffed descendants of meritorious ministers; he was granted the households of Qingxiang County in Quanzhou Circuit as fief.
translations.idiomatic: After the south had been pacified, meritorious families were further enfeoffed, and he received the registered households of Qingxiang County in Quanzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 其在中臺，務振宏綱，弗親細故。

translations.literal: While at the Central Censorate, he devoted himself to restoring grand institutions, not personally handling minor matters.
translations.idiomatic: At the Central Censorate he worked to uphold the great principles of oversight and did not involve himself in petty details.

sentences.zh: 興利之臣欲援金就制，並憲司入漕府；

translations.literal: Officials seeking profit wished to follow Jin precedent, merging the censorate into the grain transport office;
translations.idiomatic: Profit-seeking officials proposed reviving a Jin-dynasty practice and folding the censorate into the grain-transport bureau;

sentences.zh: 當政者又請以郡府之吏，互照憲司檢底。

translations.literal: those in power also requested that prefectural clerks mutually inspect censorate records.
translations.idiomatic: while others in power asked that prefectural clerks be allowed to cross-check the censorate's files.

sentences.zh: 玉昔帖木兒曰：「風憲所以戢奸，若是，有傷監臨之體。」

translations.literal: Usutai Temür said: "The winds of the censorate exist to restrain evil — if so, it damages the integrity of oversight.
translations.idiomatic: Usutai Temür said, "The censorate exists to curb wrongdoing — to do this would destroy its authority as an overseer."

sentences.zh: 其議乃沮。

translations.literal: That proposal was then thwarted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 遇事廷辯，吐辭鯁直，誓祖每為之霽威。

translations.literal: When encountering matters debated at court, his words blunt and straight — the Shizu each time relaxed his wrath for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he argued matters before the throne his speech was blunt and forthright, yet Kublai each time softened his anger on his account.

sentences.zh: 至元二十四年，宗王乃顏叛東鄙，世祖躬行天討，命總戎者先之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Zhiyuan, Prince Nayan rebelled in the eastern marches; the Shizu personally undertook heaven's punishment; ordered the commander-in-chief to go first.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of the Zhiyuan era Prince Nayan rebelled in the eastern frontier; Kublai personally led the punitive campaign and ordered the field commander to go ahead.

sentences.zh: 世祖至半道，玉昔帖木兒已退敵，僵屍覆野，數旬之間，三戰三捷，獲乃顏以獻。

translations.literal: When the Shizu reached halfway, Usutai Temür had already repelled the enemy; corpses covered the wild; within several ten-day periods, three battles three victories; captured Nayan and presented him.
translations.idiomatic: Before Kublai had even reached the front, Usutai Temür had already routed the rebels; the dead lay thick upon the field. Within a few weeks he fought three battles and won three victories, captured Nayan, and presented him to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔選誠輿橐駝百蹄勞之。

translations.literal: An edict selected one hundred tribute camels to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him one hundred tribute camels as a reward.

sentences.zh: 謝曰：「天威所臨，猶風偃草，臣何力之有。」

translations.literal: He declined: "Where heavenly majesty arrives, it is like wind flattening grass — what strength have I?
translations.idiomatic: He declined, saying, "Where the emperor's majesty falls, rebels scatter like grass before the wind — what credit is mine?"

sentences.zh: 世祖還，留籲昔帖木兒剿其餘黨，乃執其酋金家奴以獻，戮其同惡數人於軍前。

translations.literal: The Shizu returned, left Usutai Temür to suppress the remnant faction; he then captured their chieftain Jin Jianu and presented him, executing several co-evildoers before the army.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai returned and left Usutai Temür to mop up the remnants; he captured their chieftain Jin Jianu, presented him to the throne, and executed several of his accomplices before the army.

sentences.zh: 明年，乃顏之遺孽哈丹禿魯幹復叛，再命出師，兩與之遇，皆敗之，追及兩河，其眾大衄，遂遁。

translations.literal: The next year, Nayan's remnant scion Khadan Tulukhan rebelled again; again ordered to take the field; twice encountered him, both times defeated him; pursued to the Two Rivers; his masses suffered great defeat and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Nayan's surviving follower Khadan Tulukhan rebelled again; Usutai Temür was once more sent out, met him twice and defeated him both times, pursued him to the Two Rivers, and put his forces to rout.

sentences.zh: 時已盛冬，聲言俟春方進，乃倍道兼行過黑龍江，搗其巢穴，殺戮殆盡。

translations.literal: The season was already deep winter; they declared they would wait until spring before advancing; then marched by forced day-and-night stages across the Black Dragon River, raided their nest, slaughtered nearly to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: It was already deep winter; he announced that he would wait until spring to advance, then marched by forced stages across the Amur, struck their stronghold, and slaughtered them almost to the last man.

sentences.zh: 哈丹禿魯幹莫知所終，夷其城，撫其民而還。

translations.literal: Khadan Tulukhan's whereabouts unknown; razed their fort, comforted their people, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Khadan Tulukhan vanished without trace; Usutai Temür razed their stronghold, pacified the people, and returned.

sentences.zh: 詔賜內府七寶冠帶以旌之，加太傅、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: An edict granted palace treasures — seven-jewel crown and belt — to honor him; additionally Grand Tutor, Grand Master of the Palace with the same ceremonies as the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: An edict awarded him an imperial crown and belt studded with seven kinds of jewels, and promoted him to Grand Tutor and Grand Master of the Palace with honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 申命禦邊杭海。

translations.literal: Again ordered to guard the Hangzhou coastal frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was again ordered to defend the coastal frontier at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，加錄軍國重事、知樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, additionally Recorder of Important State Affairs and Director of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was further appointed Recorder of Important State Affairs and Director of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 宗王帥臣咸稟命焉。

translations.literal: Princes and commanders-in-chief all received orders from him.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and field commanders alike took their orders from him.

sentences.zh: 特賜步輦入內。

translations.literal: Specially granted a sedan chair for entering the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially granted a palanquin for entering the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 位望之崇，廷臣無出其右。

translations.literal: His eminence and standing — no court minister surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: In rank and prestige no minister at court stood above him.

sentences.zh: 三十年，成宗以皇孫撫軍北邊，玉昔帖木兒輔行，請授皇孫以儲闈舊璽，詔從之。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, Chengzong with the imperial grandson garrisoned the northern frontier; Usutai Temür assisted the expedition; requested that the imperial grandson be given the old seal of the Heir Apparent; an edict complied.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year Chengzong led the imperial grandson to garrison the northern frontier; Usutai Temür accompanied the expedition and asked that the heir be entrusted with the former seal of the crown prince — and the edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，世祖崩，皇孫南還。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, the Shizu passed away; the imperial grandson returned south.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year of his reign Kublai Khan died, and the imperial grandson marched south.

sentences.zh: 宗室諸王會於上都。

translations.literal: Princes of the imperial clan assembled at Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: The princes of the imperial clan gathered at Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 定策之際，玉昔帖木兒起謂晉王甘麻剌曰：「宮車晏駕，已逾三月，神器不可久虛，宗祧不可乏主。

translations.literal: At the moment of deciding policy, Usutai Temür rose and said to Prince Jin Ganmala: "The imperial carriage has halted; it has already been more than three months. The sacred vessel cannot long stand empty; the ancestral temple cannot lack a lord.
translations.idiomatic: When the succession was being decided, Usutai Temür stood and addressed Prince Ganmala of Jin: "The emperor has been dead more than three months. The throne cannot remain vacant, nor the ancestral line without a ruler.

sentences.zh: 疇昔儲闈符璽既有所歸，王為宗盟之長，奚俟而不言。」

translations.literal: Long ago the heir's seal already had its destination; the prince is head of the clan alliance — why wait and not speak?"
translations.idiomatic: The heir's seal was settled long ago, and you are chief among the princes — why hold your tongue any longer?"

sentences.zh: 甘麻剌遽曰：「皇帝踐祚，願北面事之。」

translations.literal: Ganmala at once said: "When the emperor takes the throne, I wish to serve him facing north."
translations.idiomatic: Ganmala replied at once, "When the emperor ascends the throne, I shall gladly serve him as his vassal."

sentences.zh: 於是宗親大臣合辭勸進，玉昔帖木兒復坐，曰：「大事已定，吾死且無憾。」

translations.literal: Thereupon kinsmen and great ministers together urged accession; Usutai Temür sat again and said: "The great matter is settled — even in death I shall have no regret."
translations.idiomatic: Then the royal kinsmen and senior ministers jointly pressed the heir to take the throne. Usutai Temür sat down again and said, "The great matter is settled; I can die without regret."

sentences.zh: 皇孫遂即位。

translations.literal: The imperial grandson thereupon ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial grandson then took the throne.

sentences.zh: 進秩太師，賜以尚方玉帶寶服，還鎮北邊。

translations.literal: He was promoted in rank to Grand Preceptor, granted the imperial jade belt and treasured robes, and returned to command the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Usutai Temür was promoted to Grand Preceptor, given the imperial jade belt and ceremonial robes, and sent back to command the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年冬，議邊事入朝，兩宮錫宴，如家人禮。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Yuanzhen, he entered court to discuss frontier affairs; both palaces bestowed banquets, with the courtesy of a family.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of the Yuanzhen era he came to court to discuss frontier affairs; the empress dowager and the emperor both held banquets for him with the ease of family.

sentences.zh: 賜其妻禿忽魯宴服，及他珍寶。

translations.literal: They granted his wife Tuhulu banquet robes and other precious objects.
translations.idiomatic: They also gave his wife Tuhulu court robes and other treasures.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以疾薨。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 大德五年，詔贈宣忠同德弼亮功臣，依前太師、開府儀同三司、錄軍國重事、御史大夫，追封廣平王，謚曰貞憲。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dade, an edict posthumously granted the title of Meritorious Minister of Loyalty, Shared Virtue, and Bright Assistance; he retained his former posts of Grand Preceptor, Grand Master of the Palace with honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, Recorder of Important State Affairs, and Censor-in-Chief; was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Guangping; posthumous name Zhenxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Dade era an edict posthumously honored him as Meritorious Minister of Loyal Devotion, Shared Virtue, and Bright Assistance, confirmed his former ranks of Grand Preceptor, Grand Master of the Palace with honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, Recorder of Important State Affairs, and Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed him posthumously as Prince of Guangping, and gave him the posthumous name Zhenxian.

sentences.zh: 子三人：木剌忽，仍襲爵為萬戶；

translations.literal: He had three sons: Mulahu, who still inherited the title as a commander of ten thousand;
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Mulahu, who inherited the title and became a commander of ten thousand;

sentences.zh: 次脫憐；

translations.literal: next Tuolian;
translations.idiomatic: next Tuolian;

sentences.zh: 次脫脫哈，為御史大夫。

translations.literal: next Tuotuha, who became Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: and next Tuotuha, who became Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: ○博爾忽

translations.literal: ○ Borokhula
translations.idiomatic: ○ Borokhula

sentences.zh: 博爾忽，許兀慎氏，事太祖為第一千戶，歿於敵。

translations.literal: Borokhula, of the Xu'ursen clan, served the Taizu as commander of the first thousand; he died in battle against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Borokhula of the Xu'ursen clan served Genghis Khan as commander of the first thousand and died fighting the enemy.

sentences.zh: 子脫歡襲職，從憲宗四征不庭，有拓地功。

translations.literal: His son Tuohuan inherited the post; he followed Möngke on four campaigns against those who would not submit, and had merit in expanding territory.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tuohuan succeeded to the office and followed Möngke Khan on four campaigns against recalcitrant foes, winning distinction for expanding the realm.

sentences.zh: 子失裏門，鎮僥外，從征六詔等城，亦歿於兵。

translations.literal: His son Shirimen garrisoned the outer frontier; he followed campaigns against the Six Zhao and other cities and likewise died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shirimen guarded the outer marches, campaigned against the Six Zhao and other cities, and likewise fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 子月赤察兒，性仁厚勤儉，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: His son Yechi Cha'er was by nature humane, generous, diligent, and frugal; he was famed for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yechi Cha'er was humane, generous, diligent, and frugal, and was renowned for his devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 資貌英偉，望之如神。

translations.literal: In endowment and appearance he was heroic and imposing; to look upon him was like looking upon a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and commanding in bearing; seen from afar he seemed almost otherworldly.

sentences.zh: 世祖雅聞其賢，且閔其父之死，年十六，召見。

translations.literal: The Shizu had long heard of his worth and, pitying his father's death, at age sixteen summoned him for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai Khan had long heard of his talents and, moved by pity for his father's death in battle, summoned him at the age of sixteen.

sentences.zh: 帝見其容止端重，奏對詳明，喜而謂曰：「失烈門有子矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor saw his bearing dignified and his replies to memorials clear and thorough; pleased, he said: "Shirimen has left a son."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor found his deportment grave and his answers clear and thorough, and said with pleasure, "Shirimen has left a worthy son."

sentences.zh: 即命領四怯薛太官。

translations.literal: He at once ordered him to head the imperial kitchen of the four kheshig.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately appointed him to head the imperial kitchen of the four kheshig guards.

sentences.zh: 至元十七年，長一怯薛。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Zhiyuan he became chief of one kheshig.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of the Zhiyuan era he became chief of one kheshig guard.

sentences.zh: 明年詔曰：「月赤察兒秉心忠實，執事敬慎，知無不言，言無不盡，曉暢朝章，言輒稱旨，不可以其年少而弗升其官。

translations.literal: The next year an edict said: "Yechi Cha'er bears a loyal heart, conducts affairs with reverent care, speaks whenever he knows something and speaks without reserve, is thoroughly versed in court regulations, and whenever he speaks hits the mark — one must not fail to promote him because he is young.
translations.idiomatic: The following year an edict declared, "Yechi Cha'er is loyal at heart and careful in office; he speaks out on whatever he knows and holds nothing back; he understands court procedure and his counsel always accords with the throne's intent — his youth must not keep him from advancement.

sentences.zh: 可代線真為宣徽使。」

translations.literal: He may replace Xianzhen as Commissioner of the Palace Provisioners."
translations.idiomatic: Let him replace Xianzhen as Commissioner of the Palace Provisioners."

sentences.zh: 二十六年，帝討叛者於杭海，眾皆陣，月赤察兒奏曰：「丞相安童、伯顏，御史大夫月呂祿，皆已受命征戰，三人者臣不可以後之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the emperor campaigned against rebels at Hang Hai; all took the field. Yechi Cha'er memorialized: "Chancellor An Tong and Bayan, and Censor-in-Chief Yebulun — all three have already received orders to campaign; as for these three, your subject cannot come after them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the emperor marched against rebels at Hang Hai and every commander took the field. Yechi Cha'er memorialized, "Chancellor An Tong, Bayan, and Censor-in-Chief Yebulun have all already been ordered to campaign — I cannot let myself lag behind them.

sentences.zh: 今賊逆命，敢禦天戈，惟陛下憐臣，使臣一戰。」

translations.literal: Now the rebels defy orders and dare to meet the imperial spears — only let Your Majesty pity your subject and grant him one battle."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels now defy the throne and dare to meet the imperial army. I beg Your Majesty to grant me leave to fight."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「乃祖博爾忽，佐我太祖，無征不在，無戰不克，其功大矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your ancestor Borokhula assisted our Taizu — wherever there was a campaign he was present, wherever there was battle he prevailed; his merit was great.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Your ancestor Borokhula served our Taizu in every campaign and won every battle — his merit was immense.

sentences.zh: 卿以為安童輩與爾家同功一體，各立戰功，自恥不逮。

translations.literal: You think that An Tong and the others share one merit and one body with your house, each establishing battle merit, and are ashamed not to match them.
translations.idiomatic: You feel that men like An Tong share your family's record of service and that each of you must earn his own glory on the battlefield — and you are ashamed to fall short.

sentences.zh: 然親屬橐，恭衛朝夕，爾功非小，何必身踐行伍，手事斬馘，乃快爾心耶！」

translations.literal: Yet you attend the emperor's kin in the quiver guard and respectfully protect him morning and evening — your merit is not small. Why must you personally tread the ranks, handle decapitations and ear-counts with your own hands, before your heart is satisfied?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet you serve in the imperial guard at the emperor's side day and night — that service is no small thing. Must you yourself march in the ranks and take heads with your own hand before you can be content?"

sentences.zh: 二十七年，桑哥既立尚書省，殺異己者，箝天下口，以刑爵為貨，既而紀綱大紊。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Sangha had already established the Ministry of Revenue; he killed those who differed from him, silenced the mouths of the empire, and traded punishments and ranks for profit — thereafter the laws and institutions fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year Sangha had established the Ministry of Revenue, killed his opponents, silenced criticism across the empire, and sold punishments and offices for profit, until law and order collapsed.

sentences.zh: 尚書平章政事也速答兒，太官屬也，潛以其事白月赤察兒，請奏劾之。

translations.literal: Yesudar, a Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue, was also attached to the imperial kitchen; he secretly reported the matter to Yechi Cha'er and asked that it be memorialized and impeached.
translations.idiomatic: Yesudar, a Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue who also served in the imperial kitchen, secretly informed Yechi Cha'er and asked him to memorialize for Sangha's impeachment.

sentences.zh: 桑哥伏誅，帝曰：「月赤察兒口伐大奸，發其蒙蔽。」

translations.literal: When Sangha was executed, the emperor said: "Yechi Cha'er verbally attacked the great villain and exposed his concealment."
translations.idiomatic: After Sangha was executed the emperor said, "Yechi Cha'er spoke out against the great villain and stripped away his deceptions."

sentences.zh: 乃以沒入桑哥黃金四百兩、白金三千五百兩，及水田、水硙、別墅賞其清強。

translations.literal: Thereupon with confiscated gold four hundred taels and silver three thousand five hundred taels from Sangha, together with irrigated fields, water mills, and villas, they rewarded his integrity and strength.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with four hundred taels of gold and three thousand five hundred taels of silver confiscated from Sangha, along with irrigated fields, water mills, and country estates, in recognition of his integrity and vigor.

sentences.zh: 桑哥既敗，帝以湖廣行省西連番洞諸蠻，南接交趾島夷，延袤數千里，其間土沃人稠，畬丁、溪子善驚好鬥，思得賢方伯往撫安之。

translations.literal: After Sangha's fall the emperor considered that the Huguang Branch Secretariat in the west bordered the various Miao of the fan caves, and in the south adjoined Jiaozhi and the island barbarians, stretching several thousand li; the land there was fertile and the people numerous, and the She ding and Xi zi were prone to alarm and fond of fighting — he wished to send a worthy governor to go pacify and settle them.
translations.idiomatic: After Sangha's downfall the emperor noted that the Huguang Branch Secretariat bordered the cave-dwelling tribes in the west and Jiaozhi and the island peoples in the south across thousands of li of fertile, densely settled country, where She tribesmen and stream-dwellers were quick to rise and eager to fight, and he sought a capable governor to pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 月赤察兒舉哈剌哈孫答剌罕以為行省平章政事，凡八年，威德交孚，洽於海外；

translations.literal: Yechi Cha'er recommended Hala Hasun Darqan as Branch Secretariat Vice Minister; for eight years authority and virtue mingled, reaching even beyond the seas;
translations.idiomatic: Yechi Cha'er recommended Hala Hasun Darqan as Vice Minister of the Branch Secretariat; for eight years his authority and kindness won trust as far as the overseas territories;

sentences.zh: 入為丞相，天下稱賢。

translations.literal: he entered court as chancellor, and the empire called him worthy.
translations.idiomatic: then he entered court as chancellor, and all the realm praised his worth.

sentences.zh: 世以月赤察兒為知人。

translations.literal: The age took Yechi Cha'er as one who knew men.
translations.idiomatic: The age regarded Yechi Cha'er as a man who knew how to recognize talent.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，都水使者請鑿渠西導白浮諸水，經都城中，東入潞河，則江淮之舟既達廣濟渠，可直泊於都城之匯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the Commissioner of the Directorate of Waterways requested to cut a canal westward to channel the waters of Baifu and the rest, pass through the capital city, and enter the Lu River in the east — then boats from the Jiang and Huai, having reached the Guangji Canal, could moor directly at the capital's gathering place.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year the Commissioner of Waterways proposed digging a canal to divert the Baifu waters and other streams westward through the capital and east into the Lu River, so that Yangtze and Huai shipping, once it reached the Guangji Canal, could berth directly at the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝亟欲其成，又不欲役其細民，敕四怯薛人及諸府人專其役，度其高深，畫地分賦之，刻日使畢工。

translations.literal: The emperor urgently wished it completed yet did not wish to conscript the common people; he ordered men of the four kheshig and men of the various offices to undertake the labor exclusively, measured height and depth, marked out the land and divided assignments, and set a date for completion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted it finished quickly but refused to press the common people into service, so he ordered the four kheshig guards and officials of the various bureaus to carry out the work, measured the terrain, divided the ground into assignments, and set a deadline for completion.

sentences.zh: 月赤察兒率其屬，著役者服，操畚鍤，即所賦以倡。

translations.literal: Yechi Cha'er led his subordinates, put on laborers' clothes, took spade and mattock, and at his assigned section took the lead.
translations.idiomatic: Yechi Cha'er led his men in laborers' dress, spade and mattock in hand, and at his assigned stretch of the canal worked at the front.

sentences.zh: 趨者雲集，依刻而渠成，賜名曰通惠河，公私便之。

translations.literal: Those who hastened to join gathered like clouds; by the set date the canal was finished, and it was granted the name Tonghui River — public and private alike benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Workers flocked to the site; the canal was finished on schedule, named the Tonghui River, and proved a boon to public and private alike.

sentences.zh: 帝語近臣曰：「是渠非月赤察兒身率眾手，成不速也。」

translations.literal: The emperor told close ministers: "This canal — had Yechi Cha'er not personally led the multitude with his own hands, it would not have been completed so quickly."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his close advisers, "Had Yechi Cha'er not worked the canal with his own hands at the head of the laborers, it would never have been finished so soon."

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，制曰：「月赤察兒盡其誠力，深其謀議，抒忠於國，流惠於人，可加開府儀同三司、太保、錄軍國重事、樞密、宣徽使。」

translations.literal: When Chengzong took the throne, an edict said: "Yechi Cha'er has exhausted his sincere strength and deepened his counsel; he has poured out loyalty to the state and spread benefit to the people — he may be promoted to Grand Master of the Palace with honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, Grand Guardian, Recorder of Important State Affairs, Director of the Privy Council, and Commissioner of the Palace Provisioners."
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong ascended the throne an edict declared, "Yechi Cha'er has given his full loyalty and wise counsel, serving the state faithfully and bringing benefit to the people. Let him be promoted to Grand Master of the Palace with honors equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, Grand Guardian, Recorder of Important State Affairs, Director of the Privy Council, and Commissioner of the Palace Provisioners."

sentences.zh: 大德四年，拜太師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dade he was appointed Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Dade era he was appointed Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 初，金山南北，叛王海都、篤娃據之，不奉正朔垂五十年，時入為寇。

translations.literal: At first, north and south of the Altai, the rebel princes Qaidu and Duwa held the region; for nearly fifty years they did not observe the imperial calendar and from time to time raided inward as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly fifty years the rebel princes Qaidu and Duwa had held the country north and south of the Altai, refusing imperial rule and raiding the frontier whenever they could.

sentences.zh: 嘗命親王統左右部宗王諸帥，屯列大軍，備其沖突。

translations.literal: The court had once ordered imperial princes to command the princes and commanders of the left and right wings, station great armies, and guard against their sudden attacks.
translations.idiomatic: The court had repeatedly ordered imperial princes to command the princes and generals of the left and right wings, mass troops along the frontier, and guard against their raids.

sentences.zh: 五年，朝議北師少怠，紀律不嚴，命月赤察兒副晉王以督之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the court discussed that the northern army had grown somewhat slack and discipline was not strict; Yechi Cha'er was ordered to assist the Prince of Jin in supervising them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the court decided that the northern armies had grown lax and undisciplined, and ordered Yechi Cha'er to assist the Prince of Jin in restoring order.

sentences.zh: 是年，海都、篤娃入寇。

translations.literal: That year Qaidu and Duwa raided inward.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qaidu and Duwa invaded.

sentences.zh: 大軍分為五隊，月赤察兒將其一。

translations.literal: The great army was divided into five columns; Yechi Cha'er commanded one.
translations.idiomatic: The main force was divided into five columns, and Yechi Cha'er led one of them.

sentences.zh: 鋒既交，頗不利。

translations.literal: Once the vanguards had joined battle, the situation was rather unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: When the vanguards clashed the battle went badly at first.

sentences.zh: 月赤察兒怒，被甲持矛，身先陷陣，一軍隨之，出敵之背，五軍合擊，大敗之。

translations.literal: Yechi Cha'er in anger donned armor, took a spear, and personally led the charge; one army followed him, emerged behind the enemy's back, the five armies joined in the attack, and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Yechi Cha'er donned armor, seized a spear, and charged at the head of his column; his troops swung behind the enemy, the five columns struck together, and the invaders were routed.

sentences.zh: 海都、篤娃遁去，月赤察兒亦罷兵歸鎮。

translations.literal: Qaidu and Duwa fled away; Yechi Cha'er also disbanded the army and returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Qaidu and Duwa fled, and Yechi Cha'er withdrew his army and returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 厥後篤娃來請臣附。

translations.literal: Thereafter Duwa came to request submission as a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Duwa asked to submit and become a vassal.

sentences.zh: 時武宗亦在軍，月赤察兒遣使詣武宗及諸王將帥議曰：「篤娃請降，為我大利，固當待命於上。

translations.literal: At that time Wuzong was also in the army; Yechi Cha'er sent envoys to Wuzong and the princes and commanders to discuss, saying: "Duwa asks to surrender — this is a great benefit to us; of course we ought to await orders from above.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong was then with the army, and Yechi Cha'er sent envoys to him and to the princes and commanders with this proposal: "Duwa seeks to surrender — a great gain for us — and we ought in principle to await the throne's command.

sentences.zh: 然往返再閱月，必失事機。

translations.literal: Yet a round trip would take two months; we would certainly lose the opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a round trip would take two months and the moment would be lost.

sentences.zh: 事機一失，為國大患，人民困於轉輸，將士疲於討伐，無有已時矣。

translations.literal: Once the opportune moment is lost it becomes a great calamity for the state; the people are worn down by transport, the officers and soldiers exhausted by punitive campaigns — there would be no end to it.
translations.idiomatic: Lose that moment and the state faces grave danger: the people will be drained by supply trains and the troops worn out by endless campaigns.

sentences.zh: 篤娃之妻，我弟馬兀合剌之妹也，宜遣使報之，許其臣附。」

translations.literal: Duwa's wife is the younger sister of my younger brother Ma'uqala — we should send envoys to inform her and permit his submission."
translations.idiomatic: Duwa's wife is the sister of my brother Ma'uqala; we should send envoys to her and accept his submission."

sentences.zh: 眾議皆以為允。

translations.literal: All in council agreed it was acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The council unanimously approved.
