sentences.zh: 既遣，始以事聞，帝曰：「月赤察兒深識機宜。」

translations.literal: After the envoys had been sent he only then reported the matter; the emperor said: "Yechi Cha'er deeply understands what the moment requires."
translations.idiomatic: Only after the envoys had been dispatched did he report to the throne; the emperor said, "Yechi Cha'er understands the needs of the moment."

sentences.zh: 既而馬兀合剌復命，由是叛人稍稍來歸。

translations.literal: Soon Ma'uqala returned with his answer; from this the rebels little by little came back.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma'uqala returned with his reply, rebels began gradually to come over.

sentences.zh: 十年冬，叛王滅裏鐵木兒等屯於金山，武宗帥師出其不意，先逾金山，月赤察兒以諸軍繼往，壓之以威，啖之以利，滅裏鐵木兒乃降。

translations.literal: In the winter of the tenth year the rebel prince Melik-Temür and others encamped at the Altai; Wuzong led the army by surprise, crossed the Altai first, and Yechi Cha'er followed with the other armies; they pressed them with might and tempted them with gain, and Melik-Temür then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the tenth year the rebel prince Melik-Temür and others camped on the Altai. Wuzong led a surprise crossing of the mountains, Yechi Cha'er followed with the main force, and by threat and reward they induced Melik-Temür to surrender.

sentences.zh: 其部人驚潰，月赤察兒遣禿滿鐵木兒、察忽將萬人深入，其部人亦降。

translations.literal: His tribesmen panicked and broke; Yechi Cha'er sent Tumen Temür and Chaqu to lead ten thousand men in a deep thrust, and his tribesmen also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: His followers broke in panic; Yechi Cha'er sent Tumen Temür and Chaqu with ten thousand men on a deep raid, and they too submitted.

sentences.zh: 察八兒者，海都長子也，海都死，嗣領其眾，至是掩取其部人，凡兩部十餘萬口。

translations.literal: Chabar was Qaidu's eldest son; when Qaidu died he succeeded in leading his masses; at this time he seized their tribesmen — in all more than one hundred thousand mouths from two tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Chabar, Qaidu's eldest son, had succeeded him in command and now seized the surrendered tribesmen — more than one hundred thousand people from two tribes in all.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，月赤察兒遣使奏曰：「諸王禿苦滅本懷攜貳，而察八兒遊兵近境，叛黨素無悛心，倘合謀致死，則垂成之功顧為國患。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida Yechi Cha'er sent envoys to memorialize: "Prince Tugtemür originally harbored divided loyalties, while Chabar's roaming soldiers are near the border; the rebel faction by nature has no mind to repent — if they join in a desperate plot, then the nearly completed achievement will instead become a calamity for the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhida era Yechi Cha'er memorialized, "Prince Tugtemür has long wavered in loyalty, while Chabar's raiders press the frontier; these rebels have never shown repentance — if they plot together in desperation, our nearly won peace will become a national disaster.

sentences.zh: 臣以為昔者篤娃先眾請和，雖死，宜遣使安撫其子款徹，使不我異。

translations.literal: Your subject thinks that formerly Duwa was first among the masses to sue for peace; though he is dead, we ought to send envoys to comfort his son Künje and keep him from turning against us.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that although Duwa, who first sued for peace among them, is dead, we should send envoys to reassure his son Künje so that he does not turn against us.

sentences.zh: 又諸部既已歸明，我之牧地不足，宜處諸降人於金山之陽，吾軍屯田金山之北，軍食既饒，又成重戍，就彼有謀，吾已搗其腹心矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, since the various tribes have already submitted to the light, our pasture lands are insufficient; we ought to settle the surrendered peoples on the southern side of the Altai and have our army farm on the northern side — with army provisions abundant and a strong garrison formed, if they plot over there we will already have struck at their vitals."
translations.idiomatic: And since the tribes have already submitted, our pastures are too few: we should resettle the surrendered peoples south of the Altai and garrison our troops north of it for frontier farming — with ample provisions and a strong defense in place, any plot they hatch will find us already at their heart."

sentences.zh: 奏入，帝曰：「是謀甚善，卿宜移軍阿答罕三撒海地。」

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor said: "This plan is very good — you should move the army to the land of Adahan Sansahai."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "An excellent plan. Move your army to Adahan Sansahai."

sentences.zh: 月赤察兒既移軍，察八兒、禿苦滅果欲奔款徹，不見納，去留無所，遂相率來降，於是北邊始寧。

translations.literal: After Yechi Cha'er had moved the army, Chabar and Tugtemür indeed wished to flee to Künje; not being received, with nowhere to go or stay, they then came over in a body and surrendered — and from this the northern frontier first knew peace.
translations.idiomatic: After Yechi Cha'er shifted his forces, Chabar and Tugtemür tried to flee to Künje, were refused, and with nowhere to turn came over in a body; the northern frontier was pacified at last.

sentences.zh: 帝詔月赤察兒曰：「卿之先世，佐我祖宗，常為大將，攻城戰野，功烈甚著。

translations.literal: The emperor addressed Yechi Cha'er: "Your forebears assisted our ancestors, always serving as great generals, storming cities and fighting in the field — their achievements and brilliance were very notable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor addressed Yechi Cha'er: "Your forebears served our ancestors as great generals, storming cities and fighting in the open field — their deeds were glorious.

sentences.zh: 卿乃國之元老，宣忠底績，靖謐中外。

translations.literal: You are an elder of the state, proclaiming loyalty and establishing merit, bringing quiet within and without.
translations.idiomatic: You are a pillar of the realm, loyal in service and steady in counsel, and you have brought calm at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 朕入繼大統，卿之謀猷居多。

translations.literal: When I succeeded to the great succession, your plans and counsel were many.
translations.idiomatic: When I took the throne your counsel weighed heavily in my decisions.

sentences.zh: 今立和林等處行中書省，以卿為右丞相，依前太師、錄軍國重事，特封淇陽王，佩黃金印。

translations.literal: Now establishing the Branch Secretariat of Karakorum and other places, I appoint you Right Chancellor, retaining your former posts of Grand Preceptor and Recorder of Important State Affairs; I specially enfeoff you as Prince of Qiyang, wearing the golden seal.
translations.idiomatic: I now establish the Branch Secretariat of Karakorum and appoint you Right Chancellor, retaining your ranks of Grand Preceptor and Recorder of Important State Affairs, and specially enfeoff you as Prince of Qiyang with a golden seal.

sentences.zh: 宗藩將領，實瞻卿麾進退。

translations.literal: Princes of the frontier and commanders in truth look to your banner for advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier princes and generals in truth follow your command.

sentences.zh: 其益懋乃德，悉乃心力，毋替所服。」

translations.literal: You should further exert your virtue and exhaust your heart's strength — do not slacken in what you have undertaken."
translations.idiomatic: Exert yourself still further and do not slacken in the service you have undertaken."

sentences.zh: 四年，月赤察兒入朝，帝宴於大明殿，眷禮優渥。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Yechi Cha'er entered court; the emperor banqueted him in the Hall of Great Brightness with affectionate courtesy surpassing the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Yechi Cha'er came to court; the emperor feasted him in the Hall of Great Brightness with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾薨於第。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died of illness at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died of illness at his residence.

sentences.zh: 詔贈宣忠安遠佐運弼亮功臣，謚忠武。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted the title of Meritorious Minister of Loyal Devotion, Pacification of the Distant, Assistance to the Dynasty, and Bright Assistance; posthumous name Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously honored him as Meritorious Minister of Loyal Devotion, Pacification of the Distant, Assistance to the Dynasty, and Bright Assistance, with the posthumous name Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 塔察兒，一名奔盞，居官山。

translations.literal: Tachar, also named Benzhan, lived at Guanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Tachar, also called Benzhan, lived at Guanshan.

sentences.zh: 伯祖父博爾忽，從太祖起朔方，直宿衛為火兒赤。

translations.literal: His grand uncle Borokhula followed the Taizu in rising in the northern frontier and served directly in the guard as a quiver-bearer.
translations.idiomatic: His grand-uncle Borokhula had followed Genghis Khan in the founding campaigns of the north and served in the imperial guard as a quiver-bearer.

sentences.zh: 火兒赤者，佩橐侍左右者也。

translations.literal: A quiver-bearer is one who wears the quiver and attends at the left and right.
translations.idiomatic: A quiver-bearer was an attendant who carried the quiver and waited at the ruler's side.

sentences.zh: 由是子孫世其職。

translations.literal: From this the descendants inherited the office generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: From that time his descendants held the office generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 博爾忽從太祖平諸國，宣力為多，當時與木華黎等俱以功號四傑。

translations.literal: Borokhula followed the Taizu in pacifying the various states; he exerted strength in many places — at the time he, together with Muqali and the others, were all styled the Four Heroes for their merit.
translations.idiomatic: Borokhula followed Genghis Khan in conquering the realm and won distinction in many campaigns; in his day he and Muqali and the others were all hailed as the Four Heroes.

sentences.zh: 塔察兒，其從孫也，驍勇善戰，幼直宿衛。

translations.literal: Tachar was his grand-nephew — brave and skilled in battle; from youth he served directly in the guard.
translations.idiomatic: Tachar was his grand-nephew, a fierce and capable fighter who had served in the guard since boyhood.

sentences.zh: 太祖平燕，睿宗監國，聞燕京盜賊恣意殘殺，直指富庶之家，載運其物，有司不能禁。

translations.literal: When the Taizu pacified Yan, Ögedei supervised the state; hearing that in Yanjing bandits wantonly slaughtered, they singled out wealthy households, loaded and transported their goods, and the officials could not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: When Genghis Khan conquered Yan, Ögedei was regent; he heard that in Yanjing robbers were killing at will, targeting wealthy households and hauling off their goods while the authorities could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 乃遣塔察兒、耶律楚材窮治其黨，誅首惡十有六人，由是巨盜屏跡。

translations.literal: He then sent Tachar and Yelü Chucai to thoroughly investigate their faction; they executed sixteen chief evildoers — from this great bandits vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Tachar and Yelü Chucai to root out the gangs, executed sixteen ringleaders, and the great bandits disappeared.

sentences.zh: 太宗伐金，塔察兒從師，授行省兵馬都元帥，分宿衛與諸王軍士俾統之，下河東諸州郡，濟河，破潼關，取陜洛。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned against Jin, Tachar followed the army; he was appointed Marshal of All Military and Civil Affairs of the Branch Secretariat, and was given command of the guard troops and the soldiers of the princes; he reduced the eastern-bank prefectures and commanderies of the Yellow River, crossed the river, broke through Tong Pass, and took Shaan and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: When Ögedei Khan attacked the Jin, Tachar marched with the army, was made Marshal of All Military and Civil Affairs of the Branch Secretariat, and given command of the guard and princely troops; he subdued the prefectures east of the Yellow River, crossed the river, broke through Tong Pass, and seized Shaan and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，從圍河中府，拔之。

translations.literal: On the xinmao day he followed in the siege of Hezhong Prefecture and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day he joined the siege of Hezhong Prefecture and took it.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，從渡白坡。

translations.literal: On the renchen day he followed in crossing Baipo.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day he crossed Baipo with the army.

sentences.zh: 時睿宗已自西和州入興元，由武關出唐、鄧，太宗以睿宗與金兵相持久，乃遣使約期，會兵合進。

translations.literal: At that time Ögedei had already entered Xingyuan from Xihe Prefecture, came out through Wu Pass into Tang and Deng; Taizong, because Ögedei and the Jin army had been locked in a long struggle, then sent envoys to fix a date and join armies for a combined advance.
translations.idiomatic: Ögedei had already entered Xingyuan from Xihe and marched out through Wu Pass into Tang and Deng; seeing his prolonged stalemate with the Jin, Ögedei Khan sent word to coordinate a joint advance.

sentences.zh: 即詔發諸軍至鈞州，連日大雪，睿宗與金人戰於三峰山，大破之。

translations.literal: An edict at once ordered all armies to reach Jun Prefecture; for days on end heavy snow fell; Ögedei fought the Jin at Sanfeng Mountain and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned all forces to Jun Prefecture; snow fell for days; at Sanfeng Mountain Ögedei routed the Jin in a great victory.

sentences.zh: 詔塔察兒等進圍汴城。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Tachar and the others to advance and besiege Bian City.
translations.idiomatic: Tachar and the others were ordered to press on and besiege Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 金主即以兄子曹王訛可為質，太宗與睿宗還河北。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler immediately sent his elder brother's son, Prince Cao Ekho, as hostage; Taizong and Ruizong returned north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor sent his nephew, Prince Cao Ekho, as a hostage, and Ögedei Khan and Tolui returned north of the river.

sentences.zh: 塔察兒復與金兵戰於南薰門。

translations.literal: Tachar again fought the Jin army at the Nanxun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Tachar fought the Jin again at the Nanxun Gate.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，金主遷蔡州，塔察兒復帥師圍蔡。

translations.literal: On the guisi day the Jin ruler moved to Caizhou; Tachar again led the army to besiege Cai.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day the Jin emperor fled to Caizhou, and Tachar again led the siege of Cai.

sentences.zh: 甲午，滅金，遂留鎮撫中原，分兵屯大河之上，以遏宋兵。

translations.literal: On the jiawu day Jin was destroyed; he then remained to pacify the Central Plain, divided troops to encamp above the Great River, and blocked the Song army.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day the Jin fell; he stayed to pacify the Central Plain, posted troops along the Yellow River, and held the Song at bay.

sentences.zh: 丙申，破宋光、息諸州，事聞於朝，以息州軍民三千戶賜之。

translations.literal: On the bingchen day he broke the Song prefectures of Guang and Xi; when the matter was reported to court, three thousand households of soldiers and civilians of Xi Prefecture were granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day he captured the Song prefectures of Guang and Xi; when the victory was reported, he was granted three thousand households of soldiers and civilians from Xi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戊戌卒。

translations.literal: On the wuxu day he died.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day he died.

sentences.zh: 次曰宋都<角┦>，至元七年，賜金虎符，襲蒙古軍萬戶。

translations.literal: Next was Songdu Tai; in the seventh year of Zhiyuan he was granted a golden tiger tally and inherited the post of commander of ten thousand of the Mongol army.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Songdu Tai; in the seventh year of the Zhiyuan era he received a golden tiger tally and succeeded as commander of ten thousand of the Mongol army.

sentences.zh: 八年，悉兵再攻襄陽，圍樊城，進戰鄂、嶽、漢陽、江陵、歸、峽諸州，皆有功。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he mustered all troops and again attacked Xiangyang, besieged Fancheng, advanced to fight at E, Yue, Hanyang, Jiangling, Gui, and Xia prefectures — all with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he mustered his full force, attacked Xiangyang again, besieged Fancheng, and fought at E, Yue, Hanyang, Jiangling, Gui, and Xia — winning distinction everywhere.

sentences.zh: 十二年，加昭毅大將軍，受詔為隆興出征都元帥，與李恒等長驅，而宋人莫當其鋒，戰勝攻取，望風迎降，盡平江西十一城，又徇嶺南、廣東。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to General of Bright Resolution, received an edict appointing him Marshal of the Longxing Expedition, and with Li Heng and the others drove far forward — yet the Song people could not meet their vanguard; victorious in battle and storming in attack, cities surrendered at the sight of their banners; he fully pacified eleven cities of Jiangxi and also subdued Lingnan and Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was made General of Bright Resolution and appointed Marshal of the Longxing Expedition; marching with Li Heng and others he swept forward, and the Song could not stand against his vanguard — city after city surrendered at his approach until all eleven Jiangxi strongholds fell, after which he subdued Lingnan and Guangdong as well.

sentences.zh: 宋亡，還師，未及論功卒。

translations.literal: When Song perished he returned with the army; before merit could be discussed he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song fell he withdrew with the army, but died before his rewards could be granted.
